title: Grave Robber | Call from Crow — Transcript

lines.speaker: The Crow
lines.text: Guardian. Hope you’re ready to get out there, because I sure am. Fielding a lot of angry calls lately. You every picture me doing desk work? … Don’t answer that.

lines.speaker: The Crow
lines.text: Eido, you can’t just — what are you talking about?

lines.speaker: Eido
lines.text: We aren’t making any progress on our own. I need help developing new tonics. Just think about how much Eramis has seen — how much she knows about Old Riis. She can help us.

lines.speaker: The Crow
lines.text: Eido, you know that Eramis has a lot to answer for.

lines.speaker: Eido
lines.text: She can’t do that from inside a box! You’re just wasting time — more Eliksni are lost every day. Let her make amends by saving lives.

lines.speaker: The Crow
lines.text: Eramis didn’t come here to make amends! She came to us because Fikrul had the upper hand. The people of this city trust us to keep them safe. I can’t tell them I let a murderer run loose because you wish she was your friend.

lines.speaker: Eido
lines.text: [scoffs] You haven’t changed! You worry so much about what people think of you. You don’t care that Fikrul is out there, turning hundreds of Eliksni into hollow shells. Or that my father is… That I don’t know how to help him!

lines.speaker: Eido
lines.text: Eramis is your trophy, and that’s all that matters to you.

lines.speaker: The Crow
lines.text: Hey, that isn’t… Eido? Yeah. That went great. I’ll get you the latest from the field, Guardian. I just… need a minute to secure comms.

title: Grave Robber | Captive Memories — Transcript

lines.text: Central Airlock, Derelict Prison of Elders

lines.speaker: Variks
lines.text: Fikrul is here, if anywhere. Scouts have found no den, no hollow he calls home. He seeks a weapon or a corpse — perhaps both. Variks will search alongside you. Fikrul knows Guardians have faced hardship, trials, in prison. He will not disappoint you by offering less, yes?
The Guardian descends into the Prison.

lines.speaker: Variks
lines.text: The Dread have come in great numbers…

lines.speaker: Mithrax
lines.text: Carrion-feeders hungry for Fikrul’s power. Do not let them stop you!

lines.speaker: Mithrax
lines.text: The Warden has locked us out of the administrative systems. I cannot assist from here.

lines.speaker: Variks
lines.text: The local controls are old, prone to errors. There may yet be a way forward.
A faint hymn echoes within the tomb.

lines.speaker: Variks
lines.text: Yes… Very strange. Variks is… unsure of the source.

lines.speaker: Mithrax
lines.text: Follow it, Guardian. Fikrul is waiting for us.
The Guardian proceeds through the Prison.

lines.speaker: Mithrax
lines.text: They shield their commander. Tear their essence from their flesh! Let their essence fuel your wrath.
The Guardian defeats the High Revenants.

lines.speaker: Mithrax
lines.text: Fikrul could storm Europa and convert Eliksni in their hundreds… why is he here? What is he looking for?

lines.speaker: Variks
lines.text: Variks hears music once again… Answers must be close.

lines.speaker: Mithrax
lines.text: More shields! You cannot escape us, Fikrul! You have him cornered, Guardian! Break him!

lines.speaker: Variks
lines.text: Caution, Guardian… Variks does not like this.
The Guardian receives a memory from the Echo, and witnesses a vision of Riis

lines.speaker: Variks
lines.text: Hmm. Skolas… he lives! [chitters] Do you see it, Guardian? Memory of Reef Wars, long ago. [chitters] Years of hubris and bloodshed. [chitters] The Fallen House of Wolves, led by Skolas the Rabid. The song… hmm. [chitters] A Whirlwind dirge. A seeking-song for the lost. But… hmm. Variks does not recognize the singer. The Echo… It is the Echo that sings to us, Guardian. [chitters] Sings of Riis, through our memories. It seeks an old strength. Strength to guide the scattered through a time of doubt and wrath. But it sees now how Fikrul wields its power… false life for an army of the slain, with those like Skolas for his pawns. The Echo seeks another wielder. [chitters] It demands one who is worthy.

lines.speaker: Fikrul
lines.text: The old Warden returns. Did you miss us? We have no need of your loyalty, Variks. Look here. You face Skolas, the traitor Kell!
The Guardian defeats Skolas, Scorned Wolf. Fikrul revives him again.

lines.speaker: Variks
lines.text: We cannot win this battle, Guardian.
Fikrul, Skolas and the Scorn disappear.

lines.speaker: Mithrax
lines.text: [growls in frustration] Fikrul escapes — with Skolas at his side. You will answer for this failure.

lines.speaker: Variks
lines.text: Not failure, Misraakskel. We have learned much of the Echo. Fikrul’s power rests uneasily in his grasp. There is hope here, Guardian. Let us report to Eido. We must consider our next steps carefully.

title: Ghost Scans: Eliksni Quarter — Transcript

lines.text: Botza Ruins, Botza District, The Last City
The Guardian listens to recordings offered by the House of Light scribe in the Eliksni Quarter of the Last City.

lines.speaker: Eido
lines.text: Hello! My name is Eido. My father is Misraaks, Kell of our House. I took my name from his first Awoken friend, Sjur Eido. As Scribe for the House of Light, it's my job to preserve our House's history, so that hatchlings may one day learn our stories. Misraakskel requested that I leave some records for the Humans of the Last City so they might learn about Eliksni culture in their own time. As he says, "Inside a Ketch, everyone breathes the same air. Though I have doubts that the Humans will care to hear our stories, the snipers who look down on us don't look like the curious types. But the Great Machine has chosen them, so I must give them the benefit of my faith. Hopefully this effort does not go wasted.
The Guardian approaches the chassis of Insurrection Prime

lines.speaker: Eido
lines.text: Here lies the remnants of Kell's Scourge — a dark period in Eliksni history. After the Whirlwind, many Eliksni were overcome by feelings of hopelessness. They were homeless, hungry, and hunted by Guardians and Hive alike. So when Siviks founded Kell's Scourge, promising to return Eliksni to power with ancient weaponry, many were drawn to his call. Though the Scourge claimed to fight for Eliksni empowerment, in reality, they represented the final degradation of our culture. A once-great interstellar civilization was reduced to an anarchist mob, led by a power-hungry coward. Let ours be a cautionary tale: no matter how enlightened a culture, there are always those who prey on our worst impulses for their own gain.
The Guardian approaches a House of Light Skiff

lines.speaker: Eido
lines.text: Many Eliksni spend their whole lives on ships. They become more than a home —they're like a member of the family. Misraaks found me in the vent of a wrecked ship, you know. We joke that my father is a Splicer and my mother is a Ketch. [laughs] After the fall of our homeworld, Riis, Eliksni scattered across the stars. Having lost our grounding, Ketches evolved from modes of transportation into permanent homes. Even after Eliksni began to resettle in places like the Reef, we never lost our reverence for the machines that kept us alive. Now, after so much wandering, it's hard to believe that there's real ground beneath us, and a real sky above.

lines.speaker: Eido
lines.text: Humans think of Ether as food for Eliksni. A form of sustenance. That's only partially true. Ether also catalyzes physical maturation and promotes molting. In that sense, it's like hormones in Human adolescents. In a world of unlimited Ether, like Riis before the Whirlwind, all Eliksni look like Captains. That's our final form. Most Eliksni you see now are underdeveloped. They're forever stunted by Ether rationing, which began as a necessity, and gradually evolved into a mechanism of social control. Now, ruthless leaders like Spider use the distribution of Ether to keep their followers dependent. If Eliksni are ever to live in peace, we must make Ether available to all, regardless of rank.
The Guardian approaches a House of Light banner

lines.speaker: Eido
lines.text: Eliksni Houses are more than tribes for sharing work and resources. They also represent living philosophies. In many ways, the House of Light is traditional: we worship the Great Machine, and we embrace ancestral roles like Splicers and Scribes. But in other ways, we're different. My father, Misraaks, is Kell of our House. But he does not act as past Kells. He does not take more than his share of Ether, and he does not punish by docking limbs. These are radical, but popular, ideas in our House. However, Misraakskel also believes in peace and cooperation with humanity. This is less popular. Everyone in our House has seen Eliksni killed by Guardians. Not just warriors, but innocents and hatchlings. I lived for many years among the Awoken, and understand that Humans do good things as well. Sometimes. But the others in the House of Light have not been so lucky in their allies as I have. It will take time to earn their trust.
The Guardian approaches an Eliksni ward.

lines.speaker: Eido
lines.text: Some Eliksni tell hatchlings that these wards keep Guardians from attacking us in our sleep. We know this is not true, of course, but it helps hatchlings to rest peacefully. Soon enough, they must learn that the Guardians cannot be stopped by such things. That they cannot be stopped at all. Even by death. After that, the ward changes meanings. For grown Eliksni, it's a reminder that the Great Machine blesses life-givers and killers alike. But now that we have seen the Guardians among their own people, taking orders and making awkward small talk… I don't think this tradition will continue in the House of Light. We no longer see Guardians as monsters. Just people: frightened and misguided.
The Guardian approaches a shrine of the Traveler

lines.speaker: Eido
lines.text: During our Golden Age, the Eliksni civilization spanned many star systems. Farther than humanity could imagine. And in all of our exploration, we never found anything more wonderous than the Great Machine. It's one of the few things all Eliksni Houses can agree on. That's why shrines like these are made of many small pieces. Each bit was added by a different House. It's a tradition that lasted generations. Most of those Houses are now extinct, and their members are scattered. It's funny. I revered the Great Machine all my life, without ever having seen it. And now that it's right overhead, I still look to this shrine for comfort.
The Guardian approaches a House of Light Shank

lines.speaker: Eido
lines.text: This Shank has been with us for many years. She's temperamental, but loyal. She's in need of constant repair, but we're used to it. Our House has fixed every part of her, from sensors to exhaust. So when I look at her, I don't see an object. I see the members of my House. I see myself. To us, machines are vessels, not just tools. This is why scrap-working is so important to Eliksni culture. It's a way of sharing our spirit with the world, even when we have nothing. I'm sure that Guardians feel the same way about their Tower. It's more than a hollow form. More than the rubble it was built from. The Tower is the keeper of the Vanguard spirit, and you would defend it more fiercely than any other building. Is it not so?
The Guardian approaches a Ghost Shell

lines.speaker: Eido
lines.text: I discovered this Shell among Spider's supplies. Many Eliksni fear Guardians but delight at your Ghosts. We think of them as extensions of the Great Machine's will. Deserving of reverence. When we arrived here, we were surprised to discover that many Guardians treat their Ghosts like equals, or worse, like servants. Guardians throw their lives away for sport, in games like Crucible or Gambit, taking the miracle of resurrection for granted. As if Ghosts needed the Humans, and not the other way around. Eliksni have had their blessings from the Great Machine, it's true, but we've never known the power that Ghosts grant humanity. I think that if Eliksni became Guardians, we would use the Light to serve the Great Machine, not our own amusement.

title: Grave Robber | Contest of Elders — Transcript

lines.text: Central Airlock, Derelict Prison of Elders

lines.speaker: Variks
lines.text: Variks detects many life signs within the prison, Guardian. Not all are prisoners. Nor are they Eliksni. Shadow Legion, Hive… and worse. Do they chase Fikrul’s power? Or make alliances?
The Guardian descends into the prison.

lines.speaker: Mithrax
lines.text: Variks. Have you regained control of the command center?

lines.speaker: Variks
lines.text: Ah… No, Misraakskel. The Warden Servitor has—

lines.speaker: Mithrax
lines.text: No excuses. Find Fikrul. Let nothing get in your way.
Central Airlock, Derelict Prison of Elders

lines.speaker: Mithrax
lines.text: I see your Warden Servitor is entertained. But our quarry slips your snare.

lines.speaker: Variks
lines.text: We close on him by the hour, Misraakskel. Fikrul’s servants fill old cells with captives. He must arrive soon to alter them. When he arrives, we strike. Trust Variks, yes?
The Guardian returns to Eido in the Last City.

lines.speaker: Eido
lines.text: Thank you for patrolling the Prison once again, but I wish you had encountered Fikrul down there, if only to confirm his whereabouts. The combined efforts of House Light and Vanguard scouts haven't been able to find Fikrul, either. Eliksni enclaves across the system continue to burn. My father is running out of time. We all are.
Grave Robber | Mithrax on the Holoprojector

title: Ghosts of the Deep — Transcript

lines.speaker: Sloane
lines.text: Guardian, there's massive energy readings surging from below the Arcology. All communication channels are affected. The Lucent Hive are forcing their way through from the Ascendant Plane. But there's something else going on. The formations I'm seeing are indicative of some kind of mass ritual to—Guardian can you read me? Guardian?
The Guardian finds and listens to memories of Darkness throughout the dungeon.

lines.speaker: Xivu Arath
lines.text: "LONELY NAVIGATOR, WE HAVE TRAVELED SO LONG WITH ONLY EACH OTHER. I KNOW YOU LOVE TO HEAR AND SPEAK NEW TONGUES. COME, SIT IN THE FLESH GARDEN. I WILL READ YOU THESE STORIES I BOUGHT AT KAHARN."

lines.speaker: Xivu Arath
lines.text: I… WAS XI RO. I WAS WEAKNESS. FRAGILITY. THEN YOU DROWNED ME IN THE DEEP. MURDERED MY FLAWS. YOU ARE OUR NAVIGATOR, OUR GUIDE. LED ME DOWN THE BLADED PATH, TO BE REFORGED AS XIVU ARATH. I WILL REMEMBER YOU. OUR NAVIGATOR. OUR BROTHER. OUR KING. IN THIS, YOU ARE ETERNAL.

lines.speaker: Xivu Arath
lines.text: [exhales] I REMEMBER THE LANGUID CONTEMPT OF OUR FATHER. THE COLD EYES OF OUR MOTHER. I SEE YOUR DETERMINATION ETERNAL. IT IS DETERMINATION THAT DEFINES YOU. CERTAINTY, CLARITY, FAITH—YOUR WILL IS A KNIFE, HEWING AWAY AT OUR LIES. YOU ARE TRUTH. WHEN I DOUBT, YOU NEVER SPARE ME THE BLADE. WHEN I FALTER, YOU NEVER SPARE ME YOUR WORDS, AND YET… I KNOW THERE IS MORE.

lines.speaker: Xivu Arath
lines.text: YOU ARE DEAD. YOUR THRONE WAITS EMPTY. BLASPHEMY. BLASPHEMY! MY BROTHER—MY BROTHER IS VANQUISHED. COURT… SCATTERED. TEMPLES, RANSACKED! MY BROTHER IS DEAD! AND HIS KILLERS HAVE NOT ASSUMED THE MANTLE OF THE TAKEN KING. BLASPHEMY. BLASPHEMY! HOW? HOW CAN THE SPEAR THAT PIERCED A MILLION WORLDS BE KILLED BY THOSE WHO WOULD DENY THE ALL-EDGED TRUTH? [weeps] MOTHER… ARE YOU LAUGHING? SISTER, ARE YOU SMILING? IS THIS THE FATE WORSE THAN EXTINCTION? WAS IT ALL FOR… NOTHING?

lines.speaker: Xivu Arath
lines.text: I HAVE DIED… AND YET WAS SUMMONED BACK BY YOU. YOU, WHO REMEMBERED ME AS WAR? OUR SISTER DIED, AND WAS SUMMONED BACK BY YOU. YOU, WHO CONSPIRED WITH HER CUNNING? SO IT MUST BE FOR NOW. IF YOUR LEGACY IS TRUE, BROTHER, IT WILL COME UNTO US AND DEFEAT OUR BLASPHEMY. AND IF NOT… IF NOT, WHAT WE ATTEMPT CANNOT BE BLASPHEMY. FOR WE HAVE SURVIVED YOU. SURPASSED THE POWER OF YOUR WILL. AIAT. AIAT.

lines.speaker: Xivu Arath
lines.text: THE SKY… IS FRAGILE. FLAWED. LIES. LIES! I SEE HOW EASILY IT IS CHAINED, BROUGHT TO THE HEEL, AND MUZZLED. THE TRUTH CANNOT SO EASILY BE BOUND. YOU SHOWED US THAT. TRUTH HAS WINGS. I TAKE FLIGHT IN YOUR STEAD. I BRING THE KNIFE OF TRUTH TO THE GRISTLE OF LIES.

lines.speaker: Xivu Arath
lines.text: YOU WOULD HAVE SAVORED MY TRIUMPH. HOW OUR SISTER'S GIFT TO ME WAS TREATED WITH SUCH CARE. SCREAMS LIKE A CHOIR AS THEIR MOUNTAINS TREMBLED. SCREAMS LIKE A CHOIR AS THEIR SEAS BOILED! I STEPPED DOWN INTO THAT WORLD, THRUST MY SWORD INTO THE HEART OF TOROBATL, AND CARVED LIES FROM TRUTH.

lines.speaker: Xivu Arath
lines.text: HERESY. HERESY! OUR SISTER DENIES YOUR TRUTH AND CRAWLS LIKE AN ANIMAL INTO THE SHADOW OF THE SKY! SHE BLEATS AND HOWLS, ALLOWING HERSELF TO BE PROFANED BY IT! SHE SPITS ON YOUR MEMORY! SISTER, YOU ALWAYS DOUBTED. BUT NOW, IT IS TIME TO TEST THEORY IN PRAXIS.

lines.speaker: Xivu Arath
lines.text: SOMETIMES, TO WIN A BATTLE, YOU NEEDN'T RAISE A HAND. YOU LET THE IGNORANT FIGHT IN YOUR NAME, UNKNOWING. THEY MOVE THEMSELVES INTO POSITION, POSTURING THEIR VICTORIES, LEAVING THEIR SOFT FLANK OPEN. SISTER, I SPIT ON YOUR GRAVE. YOU WERE WRONG.

lines.speaker: Xivu Arath
lines.text: THERE IS AN END IN SIGHT NOW, CLEARER THAN I HAVE EVER SEEN IT. THE HORIZON NARROWS DOWN TO A SINGLE EDGE, SHARPER THAN HOPE. I SEE THE FINAL SHAPE COMING INTO FOCUS IN THIS CUTTING MOTION, AND THE DEEP SINGS ITS PROMISES. I CRACK MY WHIP UNTO THE RHYTHM. I GUIDE YOUR KNIFE IN BETWEEN RIBS! EVEN NOW, ALONE, YOU ARE MY NAVIGATOR.

lines.speaker: Xivu Arath
lines.text: THE SKY'S LIARS ARE ELOQUENT IN THEIR TENACITY. THEY MAKE ME DOUBT MY OWN HAND… MY OWN RIGHT! OUR BLADES CLASH, AND I AM DRIVEN BACK, BACK! I HAD MY BLADE AT THEIR THROAT, AND THEY SLIPPED PAST MY GUARD. BUT IT IS TOO LATE NOW. EVEN THEIR DEEPEST CUTS ARE TOO SHALLOW TO KILL. I SEE THE FINAL SHAPE COMING FOR THEIR HEART.

lines.speaker: Xivu Arath
lines.text: I COME TO YOU NOW TO SAY GOODBYE, BROTHER. THIS WILL BE MY LAST VISITATION. A FINAL KNEE AT YOUR GRAVE. I'M LEFT TO WONDER IF THERE'S ANYTHING OF YOU STILL IN THERE. I AM LEFT TO WONDER… WHAT IS THIS FEELING? THE SKY IS MORTALLY WOUNDED, BLEEDING OUT. YET… A PART OF ME LONGS FOR THE COMFORT OF THE GARDENS. OF YOUR STORIES. OF SISTER'S. I LONG FOR OUR JOURNEYS TOGETHER… BUT KNOW THEY HAVE COME TO AN END. WE WILL BE PROVEN RIGHT. YOU WILL BE PROVEN RIGHT. BROTHER. IF YOU HAVE TAUGHT ME ANYTHING, IT WAS TO NEVER DENY A TRUTH, EVEN WHEN IT GRIEVES US. WHAT IS THIS FEELING? I DO NOT WANT IT!

lines.speaker: Sloane
lines.text: Picking you up again, the signal's clearing and I'm receiving your Ghost's feed of—is that… Oryx? Ugh, were the Lucent Hive trying to—this was a ritual to resurrect the Taken King! By force? We're lucky you were able to stop this, Guardian. I don't even know if what they were trying to do here was possible but… the risk alone… I'm going to contact Ikora immediately. She'll want the Hidden to secure Oryx's remains for study.

title: Ghost Scans: Eliksni Quarter Post-Sabotage — Transcript

lines.text: Botza Ruins, Botza District, The Last City
The Guardian investigates the sabotaged Eliksni camp.
The Guardian approaches the smashed Ether tanks

lines.speaker: Eido
lines.text: I believe this is the war strategy Humans call “poisoning the town well.” Luckily, we have enough Ether reserves to last until repairs are made, but this is a worrying sign. When Ikora Rey offered us refuge, we assumed she had the authority to do so. But the longer we stay here, the more we wonder if anyone is in charge of this city. Your leaders do not seem to have the loyalty of the people. This instability puts Misraakskel in a difficult position. Many in our House were against coming here, but they trusted my father’s judgment. Now, his messages of tolerance and forgiveness appear naive. Perhaps this was the attackers’ goal.
The Guardian approaches a torn House of Light banner

lines.speaker: Eido
lines.text: This “sharing of hatred,” as my father would say, is disappointing but not unexpected. Some Eliksni believe that Guardians prey on us without reason. But as a Scribe, I know better. The accusations Lakshmi makes against us are mostly true. Eliksni have raided the Last City for centuries. They were driven not only by desperation, but by unspoken resentment at the Great Machine’s abandonment. Every Kell since the Whirlwind has tried to unify the Eliksni in opposition to humanity. This war-like mentality has been a weakness. The House of Light tries to unify Eliksni with humanity, not against them. And this is how we are received.
The Guardian approaches the destroyed shrine of the Traveler

lines.speaker: Eido
lines.text: I’m surprised Humans would destroy a representation of the Great Machine. My research with the Awoken suggested that Humans revered it as we do. However, my personal observations have not supported that conclusion. I understand the City used to have an official “Speaker.” A sort of cleric who spoke to the Great Machine’s will. However, Human records state that role was abandoned after Dominus Ghaul sacked the City. To leave the Great Machine without a representative among the people seems…heretical. Many Eliksni believe that humanity takes the Great Machine’s blessings for granted. Just as we once did. Perhaps they’re right.

title: Grave Robber | Eramis Breakout — Transcript

lines.text: The Guardian hacks Eramis’s cell. The Crow transmats into the room.

lines.speaker: The Crow
lines.text: Guess Eido talked you into it, huh?

lines.speaker: Eramis
lines.text: Ugh. I have seen more competent escape attempts from hatchlings.

lines.speaker: The Crow
lines.text: It’s not the Guardian’s fault. I figured Eido wasn’t going to let this go.

lines.speaker: Eramis
lines.text: And now? Back to my cell? Or have I spent your patience, at last?

lines.speaker: The Crow
lines.text: I’ll make you a deal. You don’t do anything stupid, and in exchange, I won’t tell the rest of the Vanguard that their golden Guardian set you loose. And we all agree to pretend Ikora doesn’t already know.

lines.speaker: The Crow
lines.text: Eido thinks you’re still capable of doing the right thing.

lines.speaker: The Crow
lines.text: I’d say “hopeful”, maybe. Eido’s convinced you can help us figure out how to stop Fikrul. Fact is… we could use some help. So I’m choosing to put a little faith in you at the moment. Far as the City’s concerned, Eramis is missing. I’ll handle it. Just don’t let me regret it. I’m counting on you here, Guardian… Eramis.

lines.speaker: Eramis
lines.text: Insufferable fool. And now, I am at YOUR mercy. For the sake of discretion, let us part ways here. I will contact you once I reach Eido’s coordinates.
The Guardian returns to Eido and completes the quest.
Grave Robber | Speak to The Spider

title: Grave Robber | Mithrax on the Holoprojector — Transcript

lines.text: The Guardian listens to the holoprojector

lines.speaker: Mithrax
lines.text: It pleases me to see you embrace the title of Slayer Baron. The Dark Ether of many Scorn stain your armor. But against the dead, killing is not enough. It is clear that Fikrul seeks something within the Prison of Elders. What is it, we do not know. But I have a song in my blood, an intuition which gives me fear... That it is a dangerous weapon from our past. A memory from a long-dead House, revived in Darkness. Return to the prison and stop the Scorn from reviving that which should remain buried.

title: Grave Robber | Mithrax’s Condition — Transcript

lines.text: The Guardian speaks to Eido at the holoprojector.

lines.speaker: Eido
lines.text: My father’s condition is deteriorating. He’s not himself. His mind veers constantly toward vengeance. He questions those most loyal to him, and — And I have nothing! No answers. No cure. Only jars full of powders and a few hundred ancient texts I can’t make sense of! I-I’m sorry. I-I shouldn’t… You have enough to worry about. Variks has some troubling reports from the old prison. Apparently, there have been intruders. Someone else with an interest in Fikrul’s new abilities. He needs you over there right away. I don’t know how much longer my father has. And if a Kell of Kells isn’t there to challenge Fikrul… We have to end this soon.
Grave Robber | Mithrax on the Holoprojector

title: Grave Robber | Eido at the Holoprojector — Transcript

lines.speaker: Eido
lines.text: I… Obviously my father misspoke, Guardian. It frustrates him he cannot follow you into the field. Queen Mara would prefer that we keep any Awoken structures intact, and my father respects that. He’s dealing with a lot right now, and I know he relies on your better judgment. I’m sure the Queen will understand if we pick up a few items while we’re inside, though. There must be all kinds of useful material in the Prison of Elders. Awoken Tech, too. Bring me whatever you can find, and maybe I can develop some new tonics. I know it’s been picked over a few times, but it’s a big prison… Maybe too big. A lot of prisoners lived out their final days in that place… So much misery and bloodshed. I guess I shouldn’t be surprised that Fikrul made his way back there.

title: Grave Robber | Speak with Mithrax — Transcript

lines.speaker: Mithrax
lines.text: I greet you, Guardian. Revenant Ketches are seen ferrying prisoners to abandoned quadrants of the Reef. I fear Fikrul’s rot has infected the Prison of Elders. You would do well to hear Variks in this matter. He is not embraced with four arms, but his knowledge of the prison is unmatched. Work with him to infiltrate it. Once you are inside… Rip the Scorn apart, until the air is rich with suffering. And when I’ve returned, I will burn the prison down myself. [takes a shuddering breath] But first… see to our people. The captives. You… are their only hope.

title: Grave Robber | Eido’s Plan — Transcript

lines.speaker: Eido
lines.text: Incredible! The Echo is alive? And so is Skolas. My father told me many stories about him. Few good.

If the Echo reached out to you, actually communicated, using that song from Old Riis… Variks recognized it. Eramis might, too. She’s nearly as old as he is. She remembers Old Riis. If there’s anyone who can reach out to the Echo, help us call it away from Fikrul… Guardian, we have to free Eramis!

I know it’s a lot to ask, but… Look, it’ll be easy. I have a Golden Age relic that I think Spider will like. A kind of scroll, with many vibrant illustrations. Spider has all kinds of useful devices. I bet people ask him for help breaking out of jail all the time! We can’t wait any longer. And I know this is the right call. But if it isn’t… Tell Crow, I’m really sorry.

title: Headlong: Meet with Nimbus — Transcript

lines.speaker: Nimbus
lines.text: Hey! Guardian! I hope you're feeling a little more confident with Strand. It sure sounds like Osiris is. Earlier I asked him how things were going with the "green strings"—just to mess with him. But after correcting me, he started explaining more of his theories. In GREAT detail. And a lot of proper nouns got thrown around. So I zoned out for most of it, but he sure sounded excited, and that's what counts. When I tuned back in, he was talkin' about how you and him still gotta figure out how to actually master Strand. I think Rohan would have agreed, and so do I. Not because he's dead, and I automatically agree with a dead guy, although, it's not like he's really in a position to argue, am I right? I, Cloud Strider Dara Danu of Neomuna, genuinely think it's a good idea.

title: Headlong — Transcript

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: We stand at a precipice, both in our conflict with Calus, and in our training with Strand.

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: We will find it together. Perhaps inspiration will strike where we least expect it? Follow wherever Strand leads you. Let's experiment.

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: No doubt preparing for a siege. We must take this time to prepare as well. The battle will be ours soon, but now is not the time. We have never struggled harder against a greater evil, and yet… We know now what Nimbus taught us. All products of the mind are conjoined in the Darkness. Our obstacles and our goals are all contained within—in fact, they are the same! The same as us, the same as our enemies. What if, in trying to master this power, in trying to take control of this conflict, we've been swimming against the river's current?

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: It would certainly explain the exhaustion.

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: The question remains… how do you flow with the river?

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: Yes, and Vex nearby. A fine time to put our theories into practice.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: These harpies—there's two different types. Is there a pattern we need to find?

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: Brute force yields little progress, while careful execution paves a path towards a greater power.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: Rohan would have said… "headlong and empty-handed."

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: Perhaps our towering friend understood more about this power than even HE knew. Think on it. When did you start seeing true success with Strand?

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: When we helped the Neomuni by rebooting the power station. What did that have to do with Strand?

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: Our perspective changed, as did our approach to fighting our battles. We took a step back, saw the broader whole, and moved in keeping with it.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: So what? We "flow with the river" by planning better?

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: By seeing our obstacles as part of the bigger picture, and using the bigger picture to overcome them.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: We're really onto something here, huh? What changed?

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: To properly observe phenomena of the Light, one needs the right instruments.

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: One needs the right perspective. I think we've found it. Seek out more Strand, and see what this new perspective offers.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: Even after all that, it seems the Guardian's energy is still… stable? Is it possible the perspective shift was all we were missing?

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: Do not underestimate this moment. This is the product of humbling training, many failures, and your determination. But you've not mastered this power until you can bring these lessons to bear under duress.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: I think I know where this is going.

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: I have a challenge for you. The VexNet contains many pockets used for testing new subroutines. There is one very near you. Perfect to discover what you can really do with this power.

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: Good, good! This flexibility is unmatched. Now, show your fighting prowess.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: I bet we could go again! What do you think, Guardian?

lines.speaker: Nimbus
lines.text: I hate to butt in on your enlightenment, but Shadow Legion are on the move.

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: Another time, then. You've more than proven yourself. Calus has no idea what's in store for him.

title: Heist Battleground: Europa (Final Weeks) — Transcript

lines.text: The Guardian approaches and enters the Bray Exoscience Lab.

lines.speaker: Clovis Bray
lines.text: Back again? I offer you no shelter. Get off my moon.

lines.speaker: Mara Sov
lines.text: Xivu Arath will not release this place so easily. Pry it from her.

lines.speaker: Eramis
lines.text: My House. I brought them for safety. To live and die in peace. I promised them something more than survival. But Sol has only death to offer.
The Guardian proceeds down a chute toward the vault.

lines.speaker: Eramis
lines.text: I once hoped to claim the power of the Warmind and its creations. I believed with power, I could free the Eliksni from errant suffering. But each time I grasp at what is necessary to break our shackles, I am punished. There is no hope without suffering, Guardian. So long as the Great Machine requires your hope, it will impart whatever suffering is needed to sustain it. In this, we are the same.
The Guardian destroys Hive wards on the Mindlab doors.

lines.speaker: Clovis Bray AI
lines.text: There it is! The overseer the "Hive" sent! Gah! That thing is burrowing into my AI. Kill it!
The Guardian battles and defeats Warwatcher, Eye of Xivu Arath.

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: I know we stopped a disaster, but… I can't help but feel like we're worse off now than when we started. How did we get here?

lines.speaker: Exo Stranger
lines.text: I thought that exact same thing so many times, Ana, but… even when you feel defeated, there are little victories to take from it.

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: Yes. Think of all we have gained. Rasputin gave us the tools we needed to stand against the Witness without ever firing a shot.

lines.speaker: Exo Stranger
lines.text: If nothing else, you proved it. Rasputin wasn't just like Clovis. You taught him to be better. You did that, and it saved us.

lines.speaker: Mara Sov
lines.text: Your people are withering. Your House is withering. I know you can hear my words, Kell of Darkness. The weight of that title digs deep into your shoulders.

lines.speaker: Eramis
lines.text: This from the false Kell of the Reef? Many Awoken and Eliksni bowed, only for you to ask they give their heads, their life, to your ends.

lines.speaker: Mara Sov
lines.text: And I have lost so much for it. I am not here to threaten you, but to invite you away from a path I have already walked. You mustn't sacrifice more.

lines.speaker: Eramis
lines.text: You would leash me, like your House of Wolves pets? Like Misraaks? I have seen the servitude you call protection, and I have seen, for all your regal words, how the City holds your ear. We are finished.

lines.speaker: Clovis Bray AI
lines.text: Well done. You've thrown away one of humanity's most precious resources… and what's worse, you didn't have to. I could have saved you.

lines.speaker: Exo Stranger
lines.text: You couldn't have stopped it. You were walking right into their trap… Like you always do — with the Witness, with the Vex. But invariably, you find a way out to keep spreading that destruction like a disease. I keep seeing it, and I keep thinking you'll learn, but… you never suffer the consequences. I should've left you to die on that operating table.

title: Heist Battleground: Mars (Final Weeks) — Transcript

lines.text: The Guardian approaches the BrayTech campus.

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: Guardian, every Hive in the Futurescape… wipe them out!

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: I've felt that anger. Keep it. We will need it when we face the Witness.
The Guardian heads toward the Mindlab.

lines.speaker: Exo Stranger
lines.text: They're still tearing into the Warmind's systems. You'll have to cut your way in again.
The Guardian battles and defeats Darkblade Kelgorath, Risen From Bones.

lines.speaker: Eramis
lines.text: How many more times must we play this game? The rules do not change. The outcome seems fixed. Go, then. Spend your Dust, your Glimmer. Polish your finest armor. I'll see you again.

lines.speaker: Eramis
lines.text: You grieve for what you've lost. Do you feel that hollow space inside your chest? The Eliksni created a word for it, after Riis. We wrote poems, songs. Wove the most elaborate pieces of art with our looms… then cut out their centers. The "dead-place," humans might call it. Choose what you will fill it with.

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: I'll never look at Mars the same. I'm glad Rasputin left something for us to remember him by. Camrin and I will pick a better name than "dog" soon. I promise.

lines.speaker: Exo Stranger
lines.text: She's mourning, but… Saladin came by the Tower. They talked for a long time. I watched him put a hand on her shoulder. She was tense at first, then…

title: Grave Robber | Speak to The Spider — Transcript

lines.text: The Guardian retrieves a comic book.

lines.speaker: The Spider
lines.text: Hmph. So Scribe Eido wants to organize a prison break. I never thought she’d have the claws to defy the Vanguard. Maybe my mentorship is finally sinking in. Still, damn foolish if you ask me. Eramis was never an earner. Did nothing but spend for all those years: Ether, lives, weapons. All wasted. In time, she’ll spend Eido’s good will too. Mark my words. But… business is business. I see you have my payment. Check your console. I left what you’ll need to open the cell. Just don’t let the Praxics catch you with it. They might confuse it for the one that went missing from their vault. Now go. Let Eramis and Fikrul tear each other apart. Just… don’t let anything happen to our little Eido, eh?

title: Grave Robber | Tomb of Elders — Transcript

lines.text: Central Airlock, Derelict Prison of Elders

lines.speaker: Variks
lines.text: Guardian. After so many years, so much bloodshed, Variks regrets we must return to the—

lines.speaker: Warden AI
lines.text: Prison of Elders welcomes you. Impress your Warden, yes?

lines.speaker: Variks
lines.text: A… malfunction. Confused Servitor from years past. Variks begs your pardon.

lines.speaker: Variks
lines.text: Variks does not sound like— [chitters] Variks will fix this. For now, we continue, yes?
The Guardian descends into the Prison.

lines.speaker: Warden AI
lines.text: Opponent identified. Hibernation shutdown sequence in progress.

lines.speaker: Variks
lines.text: Opponent…? The Warden is pulling prisoners from cold storage.
The Guardian defeats the prisoners and proceeds to the next cell block.

lines.speaker: Variks
lines.text: Enough. Variks demands you initiate shutdown! Override code: Loyal.

lines.speaker: Warden AI
lines.text: Doppelganger Lockout Protocol in effect. Ha-ha-haptic interface connections — severed.

lines.speaker: Variks
lines.text: Doppel…? Prison of Elders belongs to Variks!

lines.speaker: Warden AI
lines.text: You fought, you won. Your treasure awaits.

lines.speaker: Variks
lines.text: The Warden withdraws. So must we.

lines.speaker: Eido
lines.text: We took part in this… blood sport. What now?

lines.speaker: Variks
lines.text: Servitor interference was… unexpected. But Variks will be better prepared. We must push deeper into the Prison. Decipher Fikrul’s purpose. Prevent revenant Scorn from overrunning the Reef.

lines.speaker: Eido
lines.text: I should send Petra an update. Good work so far, Guardian.

lines.speaker: Variks
lines.text: Your report — Variks’ involvement is minimal, yes?
The Guardian places the Walker technology in the tonic laboratory

lines.speaker: Eido
lines.text: Along with the new reagents you've picked up from that awful place, we might be able to develop new tonics to test on the battlefield. I keep asking Crow to let Eramis help us, but he's as immovable as a Walker inside a web grenade discharge. I've been running tonic theory by her anyway, and I think we should see some new results. Soon, I hope, for my father's sake.
Grave Robber | Speak to The Spider

title: Heist Battleground: Mars (Week 4) — Transcript

lines.text: The Guardian approaches the BrayTech campus.

lines.speaker: Rasputin
lines.text: Assessment: BrayTech Futurescape is threatened. Response: Guardian deployed.

lines.speaker: Mara Sov
lines.text: Guardian, we move to secure another fragment of Charlemagne. Make haste.
The Guardian heads toward the Mindlab.

lines.speaker: Mara Sov
lines.text: How many times has this facility changed hands between Bray and Hive? I wonder which side will relent first.

lines.speaker: Rasputin
lines.text: This is my home, as the Reef is yours. We did not allow the Hive to take our homes before. I will not allow it now.

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: You're close to the submind vault now. They cannot stop you, Guardian. Cut your way in.

lines.speaker: Rasputin
lines.text: Charlemagne. Hello, old friend. Soon, you will wake from your slumber and be home again.

lines.speaker: Exo Stranger
lines.text: That Knight we're facing—I've learned more. Their name is Kelgorath and serve as one of Xivu's lieutenants. The Hive here tithe to them. They say the Knight is "risen from bones," immortal. We'll see.
The Guardian battles and defeats Darkblade Kelgorath, Risen From Bones.

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: Happy for me. A little jealous, too… but he's always been good at hiding how he really feels. Used to be for his own benefit. Now, it's for mine. That sweet old curmudgeon…

lines.speaker: Exo Stranger
lines.text: Well, don't let him hear you say that.

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: I feel like I've said this a thousand times, but… Red, it is so damn good to have you back.

lines.speaker: Rasputin
lines.text: Yes, it is also good to be alive again. I am enjoying the company of friends. While my core processes were suspended, I was able to perceive basic vocal patterns. Your voice was calming.

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: I'm sorry it took so long. I'm sorry I couldn't… I should never have let that happen in the first place.

lines.speaker: Rasputin
lines.text: Your guilt is unnecessary, but touching. Thank you for not giving up on me.

lines.speaker: Exo Stranger
lines.text: I keep expecting to hear his voice. Clovis never missed an opportunity to admonish me.

lines.speaker: Mara Sov
lines.text: My mother Osana was the same, but only in private. In public, she wore a mask, painted with the most delicate smile.

lines.speaker: Rasputin
lines.text: Your inflection suggests… pleasure. The Guardian's performance has met your expectations.

lines.speaker: Rasputin
lines.text: I understand they are quite high.

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: Mithrax should have ended Eramis when he had the chance.

lines.speaker: Mara Sov
lines.text: The Witness would have folded House Salvation into its army regardless. If Mithrax had taken his blade to Eramis, he'd have cut only one head off the hydra… and at the cost of his soul. I suspect that's what she wanted.

lines.speaker: Exo Stranger
lines.text: Mara, any further movement on the Wrathborn side?

lines.speaker: Mara Sov
lines.text: No. Xivu Arath is… still. Like a tiger crouched in the reeds, waiting. But I can feel the promise of violence in the air.

lines.speaker: Rasputin
lines.text: Submind directory allocation established. File transfer commencing.

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: Still nothing regarding my vision? Regarding Nefele?

lines.speaker: Rasputin
lines.text: Unfortunately, I have been unable to locate key information regarding your queries, but I am able to confirm the existence of "Nefele Stronghold."

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: But… it IS real? I can't wait to see the look on Ikora's face. Everything else is only a matter of time.

lines.speaker: Rasputin
lines.text: I have flagged 38,611 potential files for your viewing, should you wish to research this lead prior to flaunting it to Vanguard Rey.

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: I may not have THAT much time.

lines.speaker: Rasputin
lines.text: Then I will prepare informative summaries.
Grave Robber | Eido at the Holoprojector

title: Heist Battleground: Mars (Week 2) — Transcript

lines.text: The Guardian approaches the BrayTech campus.

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: You're in the thick, Guardian. Hive, Taken… pretty sure they know you're coming now.

lines.speaker: Exo Stranger
lines.text: Then there's no time to waste.
The Guardian reaches the escalation nodes.

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: Guardian, I need those cleared so I can tap into the network.
A Deathtongue Chorister moves to channel Xivu Arath's Battlesong.

lines.speaker: Exo Stranger
lines.text: Deathtongue spotted. Target that Acolyte, Guardian!
The Hive send in an Ogre.

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: The Hive are sending an Ogre!

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: Hang on, Jinju, we're in for some chop!

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: Moving back to a holding pattern. Good luck!
The Guardian clears the escalation nodes.

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: Towers are ours again. Grabbing you a laser core for the gunk.
The Guardian hacks the campus door.

lines.speaker: Exo Stranger
lines.text: We'll need to open up the campus again.
The Guardian opens the campus door.
The Guardian heads toward the Mindlab.

lines.speaker: Exo Stranger
lines.text: The perimeter towers ahead are back online and reading you as hostile. Mind your steps.

lines.speaker: Exo Stranger
lines.text: Perimeter towers in range. Stay hidden, Guardian.

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: The Hive aren't switching up their strategy. What's that saying you used to like, Elsie? "If at first, you don't succeed, try, try again."

lines.speaker: Exo Stranger
lines.text: Spot on… though I might have taken it too literally.

lines.speaker: Exo Stranger
lines.text: Secure what we can of Charlemagne, Guardian, and slip away safely.
The Guardian battles and defeats Darkblade Kelgorath, Risen From Bones.

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: Elsie, how did you work with him? How did you know everything you knew and still decide to walk through those doors every day?

lines.speaker: Exo Stranger
lines.text: I know this feels hollow after the fact, but… at the time, I felt the ends justified the means. I thought my being there would make a difference.

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: But you saw who he was, even back then!

lines.speaker: Exo Stranger
lines.text: And I did everything I could to stand in his way, to curb his worst impulses. And then when I realized I wasn't stopping anything… it was too late.

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: Yeah. It can be tough to know if someone is worth the effort or not. But now I have you, and you have me. He won't take advantage of us ever again.

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: These Hive don't belong to Nokris. I know his troops scattered after we shish-kabbobed Xol with a Valkyrie, but I didn't think they'd just abandon Mars.

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: Nokris's forces pledged themselves to Savathûn. They stand with the Lucent Brood against Xivu Arath. Have you been so involved with Rasputin that you were not aware?

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: I guess no one can clear the Hive out like other Hive.

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: Consider that Savathûn avoided a direct conflict with her whenever possible. Xivu Arath is their war avatar for good reason.

lines.speaker: Clovis Bray AI
lines.text: Did the Warmind make contact with Clarity? There are trace elements in its code structure.

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: Rasputin attempted to protect us from the Black Fleet. He was unable to stop them.

lines.speaker: Clovis Bray AI
lines.text: A disappointing miscalculation—potentially even a malfunction.

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: You don't know him! Rasputin chose to stand with us. To give us hope.

lines.speaker: Clovis Bray AI
lines.text: Osiris. You were like Anastasia: immortal, commanding the Traveler's power?

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: I… was. But I have since lost my connection with the Light.

lines.speaker: Clovis Bray AI
lines.text: And yet I see the City has access to technology able to dampen the Traveler's power—even extinguish it, to a limited capacity. Surely this technology could be reversed—applied to those little drones. Imagine, immortality restored… If it could be done, think of the applications. You may not even need the Traveler anymore.

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: There was one who spoke like you. They came to the City thinking only of what they could take, and the Traveler disintegrated them. But you're welcome to try.

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: Osiris, are these time wounds on Mars similar to anything you've seen in the Infinite Forest?

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: Only in that they both provide pathways through parallel realities.

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: So it's not our past? I mean, we couldn't change anything by going into them?

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: It is a version of our past, perhaps even identical, but no. While knowledge gleaned from within them could influence decisions in the present, any actions taken would cast a chaotic chain of events into the sea of time, alongside all the others. Those bound to the chain would experience its new fate, but here… the events of our past are set.

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: I have seen this term more than once in the data feed. What is "Nefele Stronghold"?

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: That again? Ikora's spies turned up that name around the same time Mars came back, but it was scrubbed from Rasputin's archives.

lines.speaker: Exo Stranger
lines.text: I've never heard that name either, but "stronghold" designations were only used for colonization projects, or… anti-extinction vaults.

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: This is promising. Perhaps additional clues await in the information we've already collected. Someone tell Saint I'll be in my study.

lines.speaker: Clovis Bray AI
lines.text: The longer I am away from Europa, the more I understand the sorry state this system is in. You can't even hold a station orbiting your own planet.

lines.speaker: Exo Stranger
lines.text: I had suggested destroying the station with a missile strike, but the Coalition commanders talked me down. Apparently, it's too strategically important.

lines.speaker: Clovis Bray AI
lines.text: You live to tear down anything with my name on it, don't you? Without the station, you lose control of this entire situation.

lines.speaker: Exo Stranger
lines.text: And so do they. We take the bullets out of the gun, fix Rasputin, and manually realign his network afterwards.

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: Elsie, I get where you're coming from, but we can't gamble on that being ready before the Witness shows up.

lines.speaker: Clovis Bray AI
lines.text: Yes, precisely. Listen to your sister, Elisabeth—ha! At least SHE understands.

lines.speaker: Clovis Bray AI
lines.text: Guardian. Welcome to my private channel. I've been watching your impact in the field. Your execution of our mission is impeccable, without error. I wrote your kind off after the destruction of Deep Stone. But I do pride myself on hand-picking gifted individuals and elevating them. You have my attention. Continue to perform like this, and one day, you may have my respect as well. If that day ever comes, and you're sharp enough to consider such an opportunity, I may have you in my private guard. Still in service and defense of humanity, of course… but you would only answer to me. No one else. Think on my offer, so that when it comes, your answer is ready.
