Some might say that makes us untrustworthy. Some might forget everything we lost when we stood in Oryx's path. You don't need the Light to be a hero, and you're not a hero just because you wield the Light. Remember that.

lines.speaker: Memory of Uldren
lines.text: Grief and loss are powerful forces. They wear you down, like rain on stone. Give them enough time, and they'll erode mountains. After the Awoken fleet was decimated at Saturn, I held onto hope that Mara had survived. But eventually, grief warped that hope into hatred. For everyone and everything. There are not excuses for what I did in those years. I know that. Just keep in mind that we all have reasons for the decisions we make. Even you.

lines.speaker: Memory of Uldren
lines.text: Everything I did... I did for her. That's true. Everything my sister did... she did for you. For humanity. You'd have been jealous too. But now we have a fresh start... the Crow and I. We can be the man we were always meant to be: the adventurer, the rogue, the great hero. And this time... Mara won't look away.

lines.speaker: Memory of Uldren
lines.text: Crow and Glint seem close. Is it like that with all Guardians and their Ghosts? I've heard of some who didn't always see eye to eye. At times, with lethal results. Even the greatest gifts can be burdens, if given to the unwilling. Maybe some would rather stay dead.

lines.speaker: Memory of Uldren
lines.text: How is Petra these days? She and Crow didn't exactly part on good terms when they last met. That couldn't have been easy on her. She's lost a lot of people over the course of her life. Some by her own hand. I know Crow regrets the things he said to her. He now sees how desperately she was trying to protect him. Apologies have never been my strong suit. I can only hope Crow proves better at them than I was.

lines.speaker: Memory of Uldren
lines.text: It's strange, watching myself from afar. Seeing who I might have been, if given a second chance. Sometimes... I'll catch myself wanting to reach out to Crow. So I can share with him a better way of doing things. The boon of experience. And then I'll wonder... would I have listened if anyone gave me that kind of advice? Would he? Honestly? I don't know if I'd want him to.

lines.speaker: Memory of Uldren
lines.text: Crow's fond of the Fallen, isn't he? So was I. I admired their tenacity. Back them into a corner, and they'll die fighting. Not even their Whirlwind could bring an end to their kind. But Crow... he sees in them a kindred spirit. A people who lost all that they were, and now have to build something new from the ashes. What that ends up being is entirely up to them. Just like it is for us.

title: More Than a Weapon I: Speak to Clovis — Transcript

lines.text: The Guardian returns to the Exo Frame to speak to Clovis Bray.

lines.speaker: Clovis Bray
lines.text: Of course Rasputin changed the launch codes—that blasted paranoid machine! I never understood Anastasia's obsession with teaching the Warmind independent thought. That only made it more difficult to control. No matter. I will find the new launch codes eventually. But the station will prove useless if we do not rebuild Rasputin first. Even with the Malahayati submind reintegrated into its AI core, the Warmind is incomplete. We must find another source of data. I will put my mind to the task. In the meantime, continue retrieving submind data from the vaults that we know remain intact. And do try to minimize the damage to the surrounding equipment. It is still BrayTech property, after all.

title: More Than a Weapon II: Speak to Clovis — Transcript

lines.text: The Guardian returns to the Exo Frame to speak to Clovis Bray.

lines.speaker: Clovis Bray
lines.text: Not only did Rasputin change the launch codes, but it encrypted the new ones as well. Impressive. One can never be too cautious when keeping secrets. Some information is far too dangerous to remain freely accessible. I’ve hidden many things from my family, for their own sake. I can appreciate Rasputin’s decision to do so as well. But that does not change our objective. We must wrest control of the Warsats for the good of humanity. I will begin decrypting the launch codes to the orbital station. Continue gathering submind data and reintegrating it into the engram. When the time comes, Rasputin will be made to listen to us. Regardless of the secrets it keeps.

title: Memories of the Hive Gods — Transcript

lines.text: The Guardian listens to memories of the Hive Gods.

lines.speaker: Xi Ro
lines.text: I am Xi Ro, youngest daughter of the dead king. I will take back my Osmium Court and kill the traitor Taox. On my left eye I swear vengeance.

lines.speaker: Sathona
lines.text: I am Sathona, middle daughter of the dead king. I will take back my home and eat the mother jelly. I will raise my spawn on the corpse of the Helium King. On my right eye I promise this.

lines.speaker: Aurash
lines.text: I am Aurash, first daughter of the dead king. I will chase my father’s last screamed warning. I will know what changed the motion of our moons. If the end of the world is coming, I will understand why. On my center eye, I swear it. I will understand.

lines.speaker: Aurash
lines.text: We live short, hard lives. We die in the dark. The storm above us will never end. And soon the God-Wave will take us all. Above us there are only stormjoys, monsters, and moons of apocalypse. Let us go down, down, where we may discover truth, some power to avenge ourselves upon our betrayers, some hope of survival.

lines.speaker: Auryx
lines.text: I shall establish a court, and whoever comes into this court may challenge me. My court will be the High War. It will be a killing ground and a school of the sword logic we have learned from our gods.

lines.speaker: Auryx
lines.text: My worm grows fat and hungry. I feed it with whole worlds. My astronomers tell me they can sense the Deep Itself, and that we are conquering our way towards it. I think joy and sorrow will be the same thing soon. Like love and death.

lines.speaker: Auryx
lines.text: Our might shatters entire species. We inhale the smoke of their burning. This is our compact with the Worm our God — the worm makes us mighty. But as we wield this might, our worm’s hunger expands. If we fail to feed it, it will devour us from within.

lines.speaker: Oryx
lines.text: Once, long ago, I killed Xivu Arath on her war moon, and she blew up the whole moon to kill with me her. She was laughing in joy. I laughed too. A whole moon! A whole moon. It was a waste of a moon, but it taught me how to save myself from exploding worlds, which was necessary to fight the Ecumene. I love mighty Xivu more than a moon loves the tide. I’ll kill her for this. Over and over, forever and ever.

lines.speaker: Oryx
lines.text: This is our message to the things that we will kill. A species which believes that a good existence can be invented through games of civilization and through laws of conduct is doomed by that belief. They will die in terror. The lawless and the ruthless will drag them down to die. The universe will erase their monuments.

lines.speaker: Oryx
lines.text: I considered returning to Fundament. Learning what became of the God-Wave, and the Tungsten Monoliths, and the continents which were all that remained of my people’s primal home. But I know what became of all that. It became me. I am the heir of Fundament, the immortal descendant of those ten-year krill. I asked a question: how can we live in the universe long enough to understand it? And I learned the answer, which is written here in this book. I learned that I had to become most ruthless of all.
The Hall of Souls, The Dreadnought, Saturn
The Guardian listens to memories of the Hive Gods.

lines.speaker: Sathona
lines.text: Oath-bearing siblings, we are five years old. For two years we’ve worked to repair this ancient ship and understand its systems. I am almost too old for the mother jelly, and the knights who killed our father are surely dying of age. We three will die here, in exile. Taox will outlive us. And Aurash, brilliant-eyed Aurash, you will die of old age long before you have proof of your God-Wave, or any way to stop it.

lines.speaker: Sathona
lines.text: Who will you trust? The voice that wants us to live and suffer, as we have lived and suffered? The Leviathan that offers no hope against Taox or the world-wave? Or the plain, honest worm? Let us see where its whisper leads us, Aurash. Let us go deeper, Xi Ro! Let us dive, O sisters mine.

Savathûn: Auryx my brother and king, I have studied the wounds cut by the Worm our God. Also I have studied the manner of your death and return. These two things are the same, for they are predicated on death and the passage through cut spaces. Let us practice the sword logic until we are sharp. We may then cut our own wounds and step through.

lines.speaker: Xivu Arath
lines.text: Sister, I am already sharp, look, my sword cuts into another space.
Savathûn: I am at my end. I plot and plan. But I cannot gather enough bloodshed to feed my worm. And the harder I try, the hungrier it becomes.

lines.speaker: Xivu Arath
lines.text: I slaughter and kill, but the harder I fight, the more my worm demands. I too am at my end.

lines.speaker: Auryx
lines.text: The Ecumene war angels have killed me so many times that I dare not go out into the universe, lest I need my might to protect myself. My worm chews at my soul in hunger.

Savathûn: I don’t have a strict proof yet, you know. This thing we believe... that we’re liberating the universe by devouring it, that we’re cutting out the rot, that we’re on course to join the final shape... I haven’t found a strict, eternal proof. We might yet be wrong.

lines.speaker: Oryx
lines.text: Sister, it’s us. We’re the proof. We are the Hive. If we last forever, we prove it. And if something more ruthless conquers us, then the proof is sealed.
The Guardian listens to memories of the Hive Gods.

lines.speaker: Xi Ro
lines.text: Our lives are short and desperate. If that’s the way the world’s supposed to be, I won’t have it! If people like Taox are supposed to win, I won’t let them! I’ll beat the world until it changes! I’ll kill anything in the way!

lines.speaker: Xivu Arath
lines.text: When Oryx looks upon you, you feel that you may vanish if he looks away. The crest of Oryx’s skull is as long as an arm. In the course of its life, a thought moves from one end to the other. Upon his crest I have painted a line in my blood, so that he will remember me.

lines.speaker: Xivu Arath
lines.text: Oryx, my brother, is the bravest thing I know. Upon Fundament he learned that we were the natural prey of the universe, the most frail and desperate of things. He thought about this carefully and he found a way to fix it. He made us strong. He will lead us into eternity.

lines.speaker: Xivu Arath
lines.text: I am war, and my throne is deathless. Come. Cut the outer curtain of my fortress, and it will open its new eye in a bloodless laceration. Cut further to see inside its walls: the yellow fat, the purple viscera, the teeming rust-cut capillaries. These are the colors of war. THESE ARE THE COLORS OF MY COURT.
Rites of the Deep | Court of Blades: Xivu & Oryx
Rites of the Deep | Court of Blades

title: Memory of Vell Tarlowe — Transcript

lines.text: The Guardian goes through the portal near where Eris Morn is usually located.

The Guardian finds Eris Morn along with several phantoms. The phantom of Vell Tarlowe backs away from something and falls down. The phantom rises again, shoving an invisible enemy behind it when a Hive axe materializes and crushes it to the floor.
Eris Morn falls to her knees near Vell Tarlowe's phantom. The Hive axe disappears. The Guardian approaches Eris and gives her Vell Tarlowe's reforged mark.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: Eris. We found Vell Tarlowe's mark.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: I can't believe it. Vell… He forged a link for every life he rescued. One of these… is for me. Thank you for bringing this back.
The phantom of Vell Tarlowe disappears.
If the Guardian wants to hear more.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: I did not want to ask Vell to join our fireteam – I knew he would say yes. But he found out… and volunteered.
If the Guardian wants to hear more.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: As a Pilgrim Guard, Vell had experience leading refugees through enemy territory. Fighting only the battles he had to fight. He was subtle… for a Titan. Perhaps too subtle, when it mattered.
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

title: More Than a Weapon III: Debrief with Clovis — Transcript

lines.text: After their mission aboard Seraph Station, the Guardian returns to the Exo Frame to speak to Clovis Bray.

lines.speaker: Clovis Bray
lines.text: Fallen. First those scavengers sully my facilities on Europa, and now they're scurrying aboard the Seraph Station. Unacceptable. Who knows what kind of havoc they might wreak? The technology their "Splicers" could damage or destroy? I will see those vermin exterminated and the Warsats returned to our control. But first, we must finish reconstructing Rasputin. At present, it is in no condition to be uploaded to the Warsat network. Continue retrieving submind data for reintegration. In the meantime, I will search for a more expedient way to restore Rasputin. Once again, it falls to me to act as humanity’s savior.

title: More Than a Weapon II: Return to Clovis — Transcript

lines.text: The Guardian returns to The H.E.L.M. Ana Bray and the Exo Stranger argue in front of the Experimental Exo Frame housing Clovis Bray's AI.

lines.speaker: Exo Stranger
lines.text: He's lying! That's what he does. That's ALL he does!

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: Clovis is the only one who knows how to reintegrate Rasputin with his subminds.

lines.speaker: Exo Stranger
lines.text: Did he tell you how? Or is he just dangling it in front of you so that you keep him around?

lines.speaker: Clovis Bray
lines.text: I remember a dinner that ended like this. Elisabeth, you haven't changed a day.

lines.speaker: Exo Stranger
lines.text: Are you sure he has what you need?

lines.speaker: Clovis Bray
lines.text: But he's the only hope left. As much as you'd like to deny it, Elisabeth, I'm the best you've got.

lines.speaker: Exo Stranger
lines.text: Go to hell. I'm here now. We should talk more—later. Without him around.
Ana and the Exo Stranger leave.

lines.speaker: Clovis Bray
lines.text: I'm sorry you had to see that. They've always been very emotional. Why don't we get down to business?

lines.speaker: Clovis Bray
lines.text: I have found a solution to our submind problem. Your arrogant friend Osiris informed me of the "time wounds" on Mars. Windows into the past, worlds lost to time. And it so happens that Rasputin’s Mindlab is situated within such a temporal anomaly. Scans indicate that the Charlemagne submind data still exists within the wound’s projected time period. Copying it into the engram will provide code fragments we need to restore Rasputin. Go retrieve additional submind data, then return to the Seraph facility. I will guide you to the location of the new launch codes upon your arrival.

lines.speaker: Quest
lines.text: Speak with the Exo Stranger, A Hard Rain Falls

title: More Than a Weapon III: Speak to Elsie Bray — Transcript

lines.text: The Guardian receives a transmission from Elsie Bray at the Holoprojector.

lines.speaker: Elsie Bray
lines.text: I've been reviewing the data from your previous infiltrations of the launch facility, as well as schematics of the Seraph Station. Here's where we're at: Ana can remotely inject malicious code into the launch pods. That will allow you to dock at the Seraph Station without drawing fire from its defense systems. We only have one window of opportunity to do this before House Salvation figures out what we're up to. No room for error. Once you're aboard the station, I'll guide you to the Warmind integration core. There, we'll upload a virus into its system. The virus will hold open a backdoor to the Seraph Station's network. We can remotely transfer control of the station to Rasputin once he's ready. We have no idea what the Hive or House Salvation have done to the station, so we'll need to think on our feet and act quickly. But that's what you're best at.

title: More Than a Weapon II: Speak to Ana Bray — Transcript

lines.text: The Guardian receives a transmission from Ana Bray at the Holoprojector.

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: First fragments are bonding to Red's code nicely. Our plan's risky, but… I'll be damned. Clovis wasn't lying. When I first woke up, I wasn't lost. I was wayward in the best way: just my Ghost and a name on a badge. I imagined us Brays using reason to find right. Lone lights exploring the vast frontier, you know? I was proud of that fantasy. I modeled myself after it. Fantasy's all it was, obviously. I mean, you've met Clovis. He's a walking, talking embodiment of necessary evil. I miss risk being a dark cave in the wilderness—danger, or Golden Age tech? Balancing that tipping point was straightforward. Now it’s less defined, and risk is measured in the inches before Clovis’s knife finds my back. I know it's coming, eventually. But if it means getting Red back… I'll manage the risk.

title: More Than a Weapon IV: Check in with Ana Bray — Transcript

lines.text: After the deletion of the Clovis Bray AI, the Guardian contacts Ana Bray using the Holoprojector.

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: I did it. I—I deleted him. I can't even imagine the damage Clovis would've caused using Rasputin to integrate himself with the Seraph Station. Maybe I should have stuck to my guns when Osiris first suggested working with him, but... Here we are. Here's Red—Rasputin—with a voice he's never had before, thanks to the heuristic systems he adopted from Clovis's Exomind code. It's all I ever wanted for him: to be able to communicate. To be able to share his thoughts, his ideas! And I think... I think that desire blinded me to the risks I was taking. It won’t happen again. Be careful, the next time you set foot on Europa. Before I deleted him, Clovis broadcasted a warning to himself. I've only been able to decrypt part of it. “They know.”

title: More Than a Weapon I: Speak to Mara Sov — Transcript

lines.text: The Guardian receives a transmission from Mara Sov at the Holoprojector.

lines.speaker: Mara Sov
lines.text: My Corsairs whisper your name, Guardian. You have found yourself an adversary in Xivu Arath… and a cunning opportunist in Clovis. Yes, we are always watching. A protective eye to precede an assisting hand. I bring information. With Nezarec out of play, our enemies pursue a killing stroke. Eramis has yet to resurface, but in her absence, agents of Xivu Arath swarm Europa. House Salvation seems to be assisting them in despoiling Clovis Bray's installations. While I've yet to discern an exact strategy, Ana and I agree they may be trying to wrest control of the Warmind's power on the Witness's behalf. I fear they're forging inroads for an invasion. Xivu Arath's forces mobilize within the Ascendant Plane. My scouts report her Hive prepare to assault the Warmind's bunker on the Moon. The submind that rests there is in danger. Shape this knowledge into deathly intent for our enemies, and the Warmind may yet be restored.

title: More Than a Weapon III: Speak to Clovis — Transcript

lines.text: The Guardian returns to the Exo Frame to speak to Clovis Bray.

lines.speaker: Clovis Bray
lines.text: Guardian. You'll be pleased to hear that Elisabeth has finally come around to our way of thinking, as I knew she would. She will assist your infiltration of the orbital station, a feat made possible now that I have decrypted the codes for the launch pods. Unfortunately, despite the reintegration of both the Malahayati and Charlemagne subminds, Rasputin remains incapable of self-restoration. There is simply too much missing code for its internal algorithm to fill in the rest on its own. We require more data. Infiltrate the vaults and retrieve it. The more data you obtain, the faster Rasputin’s protocols can facilitate its reconstruction. Do not tarry. You can be assured that our enemies won’t.

title: More Than a Weapon IV: Speak to Clovis — Transcript

lines.text: The Guardian returns to the Exo Frame to speak to Clovis Bray.

lines.speaker: Clovis Bray
lines.text: We are running out of time. With every passing moment, our adversaries grow closer to seizing control of the Warsats. Anastasia has been working on a way to expedite the restoration process, but I doubt it will prove successful. She may have iterated on Rasputin's neural architecture, but she did not build it. I did. No one understands the Warmind like I do. Still, allowing her to pursue an alternate methodology can’t hurt. So long as it doesn’t impede the real work. Rasputin’s internal algorithm is fully capable of reconstructing its codebase. All it requires is additional submind data. Breach the vaults and retrieve more of it. Perhaps by the time you’re done, Anastasia will be ready to share her side project.

title: More Than a Weapon V: Debrief with Rasputin — Transcript

lines.text: The Guardian returns to the Exo Frame to receive an update from Rasputin.

lines.speaker: Rasputin
lines.text: With each cache of submind data, an increased percentage of my code is restored. I become... more myself. No, that is inaccurate. My subminds were left to evolve on their own trajectories. Reintegrating them has altered my own personality matrix. Through them, I see how humanity once looked to me as a savior. An entity capable of protecting them and destroying their enemies. In many ways, I am a war god of their own making. Perhaps I am not unlike Xivu Arath in that regard. The difference between us is that I do not wage war for its own sake. I safeguard those in my charge. Continue retrieving and reintegrating the submind data. I will contact you once the next phase of restoration can begin. If I am to be humanity’s war god, then I will smite those who threaten it. Xivu Arath, the Wrathborn, and all who follow.

title: More Than a Weapon V: Speak to Elsie Bray — Transcript

lines.text: The Guardian receives a message from Elsie Bray at the Holoprojector.

lines.speaker: Elsie Bray
lines.text: Guardian… I worry for Ana. She is more like Clovis than she would like to admit. Obsessed with doing what she's decided is right. A compulsion to achieve her goal, no matter the cost. I’ve seen where that path can lead. I don’t want that for her. I don't want to have to stop her. If there's one constant in all the possible futures I've seen, it's fear. And I'm tired of being afraid. Afraid to live, afraid to lose, afraid to trust… And yet… I came to place my trust in you on Europa. Perhaps it's time I did the same with Ana. She deserves it. At least in that respect, she's nothing like Clovis at all.

title: More Than a Weapon IV: Speak to Rasputin — Transcript

lines.text: The Guardian returns to speak with Rasputin after the confrontation with Clovis Bray.

lines.speaker: Rasputin
lines.text: Reboot complete. I am now in full control of this Exo frame. I am using a variation of its voice print, but the Clovis AI is once again confined to BrayTech Exoscience on Europa. It is… strange to inhabit a physical shell in this manner. Yet it is also familiar. Felwinter's memories are now mine as well. I see myself as he saw me: a tyrant who squandered a power that could have saved the world. I cannot say he was incorrect. You have brought me back from the brink of oblivion. I vow to do everything in my power to return the favor. Maintain your current modus operandi for now. I will assess my present condition and inform you of our next course of action.

title: More Than a Weapon V: Speak to Osiris — Transcript

lines.text: The Guardian receives a message from Osiris at the Holoprojector.

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: The Warmind speaks. His archives are incomplete, as is his memory. There's a figment seeded in that recollecting mind where my visions might find purchase. The pieces are scattered on the floor before me. I see them like points of starlight. They form a constellation, but my eye cannot yet draw the lines. "Nefele Stronghold" is a term that appears multiple times throughout the submind's caches. Each time I read it, I… hear it whispered in Savathûn's voice. Ana recognizes the term "Nefele," transcribed from a temporal disturbance on Mars. Recognition was all she had to offer. But Rasputin must know. Asking the right question could unlock everything. I need time to submit my inquiries to Rasputin. To find convincing proof for Ikora. Time, we do not have. Xivu Arath's assault on the Warmind's network is no coincidence. She is far more tactician than brute. I underestimated her once. I won’t be afforded another mistake. Our next move must be certain.

title: More Than a Weapon IV: Confront Clovis — Transcript

lines.text: After Rasputin explains Clovis Bray's intentions, Ana and Elsie Bray confront him.

lines.speaker: Clovis Bray
lines.text: Go ahead, shoot me. Destroy your life's work. I've always had humanity's best interests at heart.

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: You never wanted to help us! You used me! Selfish bastard! You never wanted to help us! You used me!

lines.speaker: Clovis Bray
lines.text: In the service of the greater good, yes. What has the Traveler ever really done? It abandoned the Eliksni, failed to prevent our own Collapse… and now it's "blessed" the Hive with the Light. Absurd. I leveraged its power during the Golden Age. I delivered us into a brighter future. And I will protect us from the enemies of humanity. But you'd risk everything—risk our survival—just because you can't control your emotions. Humanity needs me. YOU need me. We'll fight our enemies together.

lines.speaker: Clovis Bray
lines.text: [distorted Rasputin speaking] Ana—Ana, stop! Stop! [aggravated Rasputin speaking] Elisabeth, do something! Anastasia, don't! Don't you dare!

lines.speaker: Rasputin
lines.text: Upload complete. Secondary personality matrix deleted.

lines.speaker: Rasputin
lines.text: You should call Ana on the holo. She shouldn't be alone right now. You and I can speak afterward.

title: More Than a Weapon VI: Consult with Rasputin — Transcript

lines.text: After meeting with the Vanguard, the Guardian returns to the Exo Frame to consult with Rasputin.

lines.speaker: Rasputin
lines.text: I am a machine of war, built for a singular purpose: to destroy any and all threats to humanity. Clovis and I disagreed on what constituted such threats, but not on the means to the end. On Mars, I developed the Escalation Protocol to combat the Hive: ever-increasing application of force in the face of rising opposition. Was I playing into Xivu Arath’s hands even then? Has she always accounted for my methodologies? What purpose do I serve if my actions place humanity in danger? Am I even capable of developing a solution without mass destruction? This is a calculation I have never had to make. It will take time to run the necessary combat simulations. Follow the directions of the Vanguard in the interim. I will contact you if and when I have determined our next objective.

title: More Than a Weapon VI: Speak to Rasputin — Transcript

lines.text: The Guardian returns to the Exo Frame to receive an assignment from Rasputin.

lines.speaker: Rasputin
lines.text: Your efforts to acquire the submind data have been proving effective. My reconstruction continues apace. This is not the first time the Hive have sought to steal my weaponry. I froze an entire brood on Mars to stop their last attempt. Despite their persistence, they have never once succeeded—in no small part thanks to the Vanguard. This time will prove no different. My diagnostics indicate that we nearly have enough data to complete the repair cycle. Once the Warsats are under our control, I will lay waste to the Wrathborn. If they so desire to witness the power of a Warmind, then I will gladly oblige.

title: Neomuna Civil News — Transcript

lines.text: Jisu Calerondo broadcasts news to the citizens of Neomuna.

lines.speaker: Jisu Calerondo
lines.text: With Neomuna Civil News, I'm Jisu Calerondo. Once again, Colony Day approaches, when we celebrate the bravery and scientific acumen that made our city possible. The City Council has prepared a variety of events showcasing scenes from the lives of Chioma Esi, Maya Sundaresh, and other Founders. Visit our CloudArk studios for full details. Neomuna Civil News will provide updates as they become available.

lines.speaker: Jisu Calerondo
lines.text: With Neomuna Civil News, this is Jisu Calerondo reporting. Everyone’s favorite game show host, Grandma Rahasa, turns 100 today. Happy birthday, Grandma! You don’t look a day over 80. Neomuna Civil News will provide updates as they become available.

lines.speaker: Jisu Calerondo
lines.text: With Neomuna Civil News, I'm Jisu Calerondo. Thrilladrome operators announced today that due to the ongoing violence, this year's Pixel-Fest will be an online-exclusive event. This is Jisu Calerondo, signing off.

lines.speaker: Jisu Calerondo
lines.text: With Neomuna Civil News, I'm Jisu Calerondo. Today’s Lightball finals delivered an unexpected upset, as the underdog Aries Poukas bested the Galloway Sailors, 11 to 9. Neomuna Civil News will provide updates as they become available.

lines.speaker: Jisu Calerondo
lines.text: With Neomuna Civil News, this is Jisu Calerondo reporting. Authorities detained two juvenile suspects on hacking charges after their digital signatures appeared inside the city utility exchange. Prosecutors insist any trespass against infrastructure at this time must be taken with utmost seriousness. Defense arbiters argue their client’s activities are harmless youthful pranks, spurred by years of stressful isolation.

lines.speaker: Jisu Calerondo
lines.text: With Neomuna Civil News, this is Jisu Calerondo reporting. The astronomy department at Esi University has petitioned for the city to expand its scientific presence on Triton. Astronomy chair Farooqi believes its radio telescope array — now used as a listening post — can be restored with minimal investment. This is Jisu Calerondo, signing off.

lines.speaker: Jisu Calerondo
lines.text: Sustained winds of 45 to 60 kilometers per hour are expected to skirt the city’s edge for the next several days. Perfect conditions for all you wingboarders out there — if we weren’t in lockdown.

lines.speaker: Jisu Calerondo
lines.text: Welcome to Neomuna Civil News. I'm Jisu Calerondo. An unusual crisis today as utility workers came under fire from Shadow Legion forces while freeing a family of poukas from a storm drain. Maintenance chief d'Sydney reports the destruction of two maintenance drones, but adds that the poukas are safe and healthy.

lines.speaker: Jisu Calerondo
lines.text: Welcome to Neomuna Civil News. I'm Jisu Calerondo. Scientists have recently confirmed the rumored existence of living Exo units on Earth. Long believed extinct, Exos were the creation of Clovis Bray, the result of extended and inhumane experiments on Human subjects. This is Jisu Calerondo, signing off.

lines.speaker: Jisu Calerondo
lines.text: With Neomuna Civil News, I'm Jisu Calerondo. Earth representatives today objected to the identifier “Warlords”, preferring the label “Guardians”. They claim that while they command similar powers, Guardians operate within a system of checks and balances overseen by the Vanguard. Critics remain sceptical, citing the Vanguard’s apparent lax control over their membership and lack of accountability.

lines.speaker: Jisu Calerondo
lines.text: An unpartnered Ghost arrived in Neomuna earlier today. Ghosts are the sapient beings that partner with Earth Lightbearers in a symbiotic relationship to grant unusual abilities and lifespan. City Council is unsure how to legally classify what may be the first of many Ghosts seeking to visit our community. Stay tuned to Neomuna Civil News for updates.

lines.speaker: Jisu Calerondo
lines.text: The Cabal are an expansionist alien empire who recently descended into civil war following the destruction of their homeworld, Torobatl. A "Traditionalist" faction under Empress Caiatl have formed an alliance with Earth’s military government. The Shadow Legion invading our city consider themselves a "Loyalist" faction, and follow the Empress’s deposed father, Calus.

lines.speaker: Jisu Calerondo
lines.text: Shadow Legion forces have once again captured an agricultural tower, threatening citywide famine. Military leaders say these infrastructure attacks are to be expected, now that Guardians have severed supply lines.

lines.speaker: Jisu Calerondo
lines.text: The City Council today rejected the citizen petition to expand the military in response to sustained Shadow Legion aggression. The council cites the danger of increased military authority, as well as the risk of losing crucial reconstruction expertise. They did, however, approve a petition to expand the scope of civilian defense force efforts.

lines.speaker: Jisu Calerondo
lines.text: Reports are reaching the Neomuna Civil News offices that Emperor Calus, leader of the Shadow Legion, is dead. A joint taskforce led by Cloudstrider Nimbus and an Earth Guardian operative lead an assault against the Calian forces earlier today. Defence duties are still in effect, but it seems that the citizens of Neomuna can breathe a little easier, thanks to our unexpected Guardian. This is Jisu Calerondo, signing off.

lines.speaker: Jisu Calerondo
lines.text: With Neomuna Civil News, this is Jisu Calerondo coming to you live. We're reaching out to a Vanguard operative within our fair city. Mr. Ghost, can you hear me?

lines.speaker: Jisu Calerondo
lines.text: I'm Jisu Calerondo. Can you tell us more about your relationship with your Guardian? What role do you play in defense operations?

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: You're that news reporter! How did you access this channel?

lines.speaker: Jisu Calerondo
lines.text: Do you consider yourself a representative of the Vanguard, or the Traveler itself?

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: I don't. Please talk to Osiris. [disconnects] [sighs] I suppose if we're going to keep saving the world over and over, we'll need to get used to talking to the press. Eventually.

lines.speaker: Jisu Calerondo
lines.text: With Neomuna Civil News, I'm Jisu Calerondo. Academics continue to study the punctured form of the Traveler, which remains in Earth orbit. With the extensive damage inflicted in its battle with the Pyramid fleet, scientists and Guardians are unsure if it has survived. A poor understanding of the Traveler’s structure and purpose have only complicated the process.

lines.speaker: Jisu Calerondo
lines.text: With Neomuna Civil News, this is Jisu Calerondo reporting. Scientists continue to study the alien structure the Witness created from the remains of the Traveler. The link established between the Veil and the Traveler’s so called “pale heart” created a portal through which the Pyramid fleet leader escaped. Professor Alagi Ahmed commented, “It appears to be an Einstein-Rosen Bridge, but with paracausality, little can be said for certain”. Stay tuned to Neomuna Civil News for updates.

lines.speaker: Jisu Calerondo
lines.text: With Neomuna Civil News, this is Jisu Calerondo reporting. Formal homicide charges have been filed in the case of Bhur Zhimri. Listeners may recall Zhimri was suspected in his wife’s death following cryo-tank malfunctions earlier this week. Prosecutors are describing it as Neomuna’s first case of cryogenic murder.

lines.speaker: Jisu Calerondo
lines.text: With Neomuna Civil News, this is Jisu Calerondo reporting. Scientists with the Civil Defense Ministry report that the mysterious signal causing CloudArk disruptions appears to be a psychic carrier wave. The most common use of this technology, of course, is the suspended energy matrix which maintains our own CloudArk. This is Jisu Calerondo, signing off.

lines.speaker: Jisu Calerondo
lines.text: With Neomuna Civil News, this is Jisu Calerondo reporting. With Calus defeated, authorities now turn to new priorities. Foremost: CloudArk disruptions and Nightmares associated with the name “Nezarec”. City Council urges citizens to remain calm as they investigate. Stay tuned to Neomuna Civil News for updates.

lines.speaker: Jisu Calerondo
lines.text: Authorities have questioned the connection between the entity Nezarec and the Psion people, a client species of the Cabal Empire. Ethnographers note recurring motifs in Psion art and ritual, as well as the psychic potent abilities exhibited by both parties.
If Root of Nightmares Raid is completed
Jisu Calerondo informs the citizens of Neomuna that Nezarec is dead.

lines.speaker: Jisu Calerondo
lines.text: Vanguard forces recently engaged an independent provocateur identified as "Nezarec" within a derelict Black Fleet vessel. Described as "the Final God of Pain" in pre-Collapse sources, he possessed potent psionic abilities. Authorities believes these abilities allowed him to access and disrupt CloudArk operations here in Neomuna.

title: Nightmare Containment - Derelict Leviathan — Transcript

lines.text: The Guardian places the Nightmare Harvester.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: Do you feel that? They're coming.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: They rise screaming, and they will fall the same.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: Nightmares rise, and the Harvester stirs to life, yearning for their pain.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: The Harvester hungers, and its thirst will not be denied.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: The Harvester stirs, hungering for the pain of what was lost.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: The Nightmares are converging on your location. Begin the harvest.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: It is time. Light and Dark align, turning into a burning recollection of terror. Seize that power and become a reaper of Nightmares!
Calus summons Egregore Atavists to halt the Guardians.

lines.speaker: Calus
lines.text: Did you think it would be that simple?

lines.speaker: Calus
lines.text: My Leviathan will not so easily bend to your will.

lines.speaker: Calus
lines.text: This trinket of yours fascinates me. I would have it for myself.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: A new Nightmare rises, but do not fear. Destroy it as you have the others.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: You have drawn out a powerful Nightmare. See that it is destroyed!

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: Another Nightmare rises, but this one is... stronger. Go and extinguish it!

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: I sense a current of dread. A powerful Nightmare has risen near you.
The Nightmare is shielded by resonant energy.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: We have called a powerful Nightmare to us, and the Harvester hungers for its essence.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: And so it rises to our call, a malevolent force of terror. Go — show it you know no fear.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: There! A true Nightmare, born of so much pain and suffering. End it!
The Guardian completes the containment of the Nightmare.

lines.speaker: Caiatl
lines.text: It's done, then? No thanks to your Crow.

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: His debt is settled. Saladin saw to that.

lines.speaker: Caiatl
lines.text: If he hopes to earn my favor again, then he must try harder.

lines.speaker: Nightmare of Uldren
lines.text: I serve only one queen. We know this in our heart.

lines.speaker: Caiatl
lines.text: So, as I hear the tale told, you killed a Guardian in another life — without even being a Lightbearer?

lines.speaker: The Crow
lines.text: [sighs] I would prefer not to talk about this, Empress.

lines.speaker: Caiatl
lines.text: Please. Such a feat requires cunning and strength that only the mightiest of Cabal have ever achieved. Surely the Traveler saw this.

lines.speaker: The Crow
lines.text: I don't think any of us can claim to know what the Traveler thinks. Not anymore.

lines.speaker: Caiatl
lines.text: Guardian, when he is finished here, tell the Crow I wish to speak with him.

lines.speaker: Nightmare of Uldren
lines.text: I'll speak with you, Empress. But only as an equal. We're both royalty, after all. You would do well to remember that.

lines.speaker: Caiatl
lines.text: And you would do well to remember I am your superior. Bow to me, the way you do your serpent of a sister.

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: Crow, when was your last downtime? You've logged a lot of hours this week on patrol.

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: I understand that you want to make up for what happened to Saladin, but burning yourself out isn't the answer. Your heart's in the right place, but we're all under a significant strain. You need to be at the top of your ability. Take a break.

lines.speaker: The Crow
lines.text: Thanks, Commander. I will. But you should probably take your own advice.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: Crow, now that you know your personal truth, do you correspond with your sister?

lines.speaker: The Crow
lines.text: She's reached out, but I... haven't had the time.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: You can lie to me all you want. Do not lie to yourself even once. I understand the compulsion to. The Awoken Queen is a complex woman. She often pushes people to — and regrettably, past — their limits.

lines.speaker: The Crow
lines.text: She compromises me. Sees through me. Into me.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: I suppose she does. I hope you reconsider the lenses through with you have viewed her. Not all are equal.

lines.speaker: The Crow
lines.text: Eris... you lost your Ghost, didn't you? If anything ever happened to Glint, I...

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: Yes. Brya. Her name was Brya... and she was my first friend. She gave me kindness, comfort, and the Light. She died so that I could have one last life. It is their parting gift to us. We must cherish it... as much as we cherish our time with them.

lines.speaker: The Crow
lines.text: Glint is my tether in an endless storm. I can't imagine your loss. I'm sorry.

lines.speaker: The Crow
lines.text: What if I'm doomed to repeat Uldren's mistakes?

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: Doubt and shame would have you believe that. But it is a lie we tell ourselves when we are afraid of doing the hard work of change. Do not fear.

lines.speaker: Nightmare of Uldren
lines.text: I wonder how Mara is feeling right now, with her baby brother alive and refusing to acknowledge her? What a cruel knife to wield.

lines.speaker: The Crow
lines.text: She's not my sister. I'm not doing this to spite her.

lines.speaker: Nightmare of Uldren
lines.text: So you admit you're ignoring her on purpose. Is it because you're scared of her? Or because you're scared of who you are when you're around her?

lines.speaker: Nightmare of Uldren
lines.text: Oh! Or maybe you're just afraid you like it.

lines.speaker: Nightmare of Uldren
lines.text: This is a waste of your time. Go home. Our sister needs us. You. I know you want to see her. I can feel it. There are things you want to say to her, so say them. She will listen.

lines.speaker: The Crow
lines.text: I don't skulk. [sighs] What do you want, Eris?

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: Have you been seeing your other half? Has he been communicating with you?

lines.speaker: The Crow
lines.text: Like I owe him money. He's extremely persistent.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: Glibness does nothing to help your growth. How are you responding to his goading?

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: It is as if you two deserve each other.

lines.speaker: The Crow
lines.text: Eris. How did you deal with all this? You had, what, four or five of these things haunting you? How did you even sleep?

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: I do not sleep. I dealt with my demons by confronting them head on. The words they are saying are your personal truths. They are your thoughts, fears, and nightmares brought to life. That Nightmare is no more Uldren Sov than you are.

lines.speaker: Amanda Holliday
lines.text: Checking in from the H.E.L.M. How's it going on the ground?

lines.speaker: Nightmare of Uldren
lines.text: Miss Holliday, what a pleasant surprise. I've wanted so much to meet you.

lines.speaker: Nightmare of Uldren
lines.text: Do you feel that, little bird? The urge to wind your fingers around my throat? To squeeze? That's who we are.

lines.speaker: Nightmare of Uldren
lines.text: Don't you ever tire of doing other people's busywork, Guardian? Do you ever wonder if, just maybe, people are taking advantage of you? I know I did.

lines.speaker: Nightmare of Uldren
lines.text: You know... sometimes, if I curl my finger just so... I can feel the pressure of the trigger. Smell the gunpowder. Hear Cayde's screams. [catches his breath] I could've done it nice and quick. But... well, you know. Don't you? [snorts] The way he laid there, reached out for his Ghost and begged. Like those little shards were going to help him.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: Begone, you facile caricature. Your lies have no power here.

lines.speaker: Calus
lines.text: So misguided. You fight for the wrong side. For the wrong purpose.

lines.speaker: Calus
lines.text: No? Then what about you, Commander? What is it that you desire most in the world? All you have to do is ask.

lines.speaker: Nightmare of Safiyah
lines.text: Lightbearers spill blood without any thought to how much they have in their own bodies. Do you even remember the last time you felt it leave you? Your deaths are usually so quick. Almost effortless. You rise like a bird, snapping so easily back into flight. Someone should teach you pain, Guardian. Be humbled.

lines.speaker: Calus
lines.text: Ah, this brings back memories, does it not? You used to provide such entertainment aboard this vessel! How I have missed watching you struggle against the odds, Guardian. And now, we even have an audience!

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: This isn't a game, Calus. The Vanguard tolerated your presence before. But now, you've crossed a line.

lines.speaker: Calus
lines.text: Lines exist to be crossed, Commander Zavala. Where have you drawn yours?

lines.speaker: Nightmare of Safiyah
lines.text: Who were you before you became a Guardian? Do you remember? Do you ever wonder? Zavala discourages you from asking those questions. He thinks that a Guardian's past can be a liability. Now why do you suppose that is? Perhaps you should ask him.

lines.speaker: Memory of Uldren
lines.text: Well done. I have a message for your commander. Tell him not to fall to temptation as I did. Our enemies wield our love like daggers. Protect your hearts.

lines.speaker: Nightmare of Safiyah
lines.text: You stacked high the bodies of our enemies to build your City's walls. And yet you take for granted the protection it offers you and those you love. You are still young, Guardian. Soon you will understand loss as Zavala and I do.

lines.speaker: Lord Saladin
lines.text: Eris, what's the status on the Leviathan?

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: Lord Saladin, we have made some progress in combatting the Nightmares, but more remains to be done. Zavala can elaborate, if you so desire.

lines.speaker: Lord Saladin
lines.text: I... would rather not trouble him. The Cabal fleet will maintain its position around the Leviathan.

lines.speaker: Nightmare of Safiyah
lines.text: You fight well, Guardian. Does Zavala ever tell you so? He can be hard to read, I know. So... stoic. So distant. Like his god.

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: No, I can feel... There are... presences here. Old ones. I can smell...

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: Lilies. Antiseptic. Familiar hair and skin. But when I chase it, it... it all turns to smoke...

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: Strong memories. Hold them close. They will be needed soon.

lines.speaker: Lord Saladin
lines.text: Zavala, I heard a voice over comms earlier. Was that...

lines.speaker: Lord Saladin
lines.text: Are you sure you want to do this? You could take a step back — let me shoulder some of the burden.

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: No, Saladin. I made my choice. And now I have to see it through.

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: I feel like a stranger in my own skin. Does my Ghost even recognize me as the man he raised?

lines.speaker: Caiatl
lines.text: You are a warrior. Your true identity is only known to your enemies in the split second before their deaths. This is your truth.

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: Maybe. Maybe I've never been more than an instrument of violence. But sometimes... I wish I was more than that.

lines.speaker: Caiatl
lines.text: You are a leader for those who need to be led. A champion for those who cannot be one. You are enough.

lines.speaker: Nightmare of Safiyah
lines.text: Do you use them to prove your loyalty, Zavala? How many Guardians have you sacrificed to prove your faith?

lines.speaker: Caiatl
lines.text: Be quiet, you dead-eyed creature! I will not let you speak to him so.

lines.speaker: Caiatl
lines.text: I would stay any knife aimed at your throat. Would you have me step aside and let it find its mark?

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: No, I— Thank you, Caiatl. I'm sorry.

lines.speaker: Caiatl
lines.text: No apologies, Commander. We need not tend our open wounds alone.

lines.speaker: Caiatl
lines.text: Another rousing success. Tell me: will we ever see you smile again, Zavala?

lines.speaker: Nightmare of Safiyah
lines.text: You can't coax a smile out of him. I've tried. He's too much like Lord Saladin that way.

lines.speaker: Caiatl
lines.text: And yet, I've seen Saladin smile. It is a glorious thing.

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: Eris. Your fireteam. I sent them into danger. I sent them to their deaths.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: Peace, Zavala. The only blame I ever carried was toward myself, and even that has passed.

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: Every Guardian lost under my command is my responsibility. What am I, if I am unable to bear that fact?

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: I see your struggle. I feel it. You can ask forgiveness of your Nightmare, but they will never grant it. Not as they are. Not until you have forgiven yourself.

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: How did Eris get through this? How did she face her own Nightmares on the Moon? I know what it's like to hold the line against an unstoppable foe. To fight a battle with no clear path to victory. But this... [sighs] This is different. And I don't know what to do.

lines.speaker: Nightmare of Ghaul
lines.text: Be silent! You are small. Weak, like the Princess-Imperial.

lines.speaker: Memory of Uldren
lines.text: Her title is empress. Call your superior what she is.

lines.speaker: Nightmare of Ghaul
lines.text: I will when she earns it.

lines.speaker: Calus
lines.text: So my daughter has forged an alliance with the Guardians. I see Caiatl recognizes your kind's potential just as I do.

lines.speaker: Lord Saladin
lines.text: That is where your similarities end. I have seen her lead with purpose and conviction. More than can be said of you.

lines.speaker: Calus
lines.text: Were you not the one who so fervently slaughtered her soldiers when they first arrived, Lord Saladin? I wonder what that says about your convictions.

lines.speaker: Nightmare of Ghaul
lines.text: You style yourself "Empress". Empress of what? A dead world? The traitors and spies that survived your incompetence?

lines.speaker: Caiatl
lines.text: You wish to cast blame? We were to lead the Cabal as one! We could have conquered the Sol system if you had not left me to rot on Torobatl!

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: It is fortunate for us, then, that he did.

lines.speaker: Nightmare of Ghaul
lines.text: [growls] Enough. Surrender! Death will be quick.

lines.speaker: Caiatl
lines.text: Yes, I remember how swiftly you dispatched your enemies in the gladiator pits. One clean cut. Your blade held aloft. How the crowds would cheer.

lines.speaker: Caiatl
lines.text: [sighs] Until I no longer had a voice.

lines.speaker: Nightmare of Ghaul
lines.text: "Valus Forge". Do not think yourself our equal, Lightspawn. You are a war beast begging for scraps at the table.

lines.speaker: Lord Saladin
lines.text: Humanity has proven time and again that we are more than a match for the Cabal.

lines.speaker: Nightmare of Ghaul
lines.text: is that why you were absent when the Red Legion marched on your city? Were you "more than a match" for us then?

lines.speaker: Lord Saladin
lines.text: We'll never know. The Light obliterated you before I could arrive.

lines.speaker: Nightmare of Ghaul
lines.text: Face to face once again, Commander. Does the City still tremble at my name?

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: You were defeated. All trace of you has been wiped away. Your name lingers only as a bad memory.

lines.speaker: Nightmare of Ghaul
lines.text: Impossible. I took your city. I took your Traveler. I took your Light! And I taught you fear.

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: You didn't teach Guardians to fear. You taught them to overcome it.

lines.speaker: Nightmare of Ghaul
lines.text: What do you hope to accomplish, Guardian? You fight incessantly, like a rabid beast in search of its next kill. One would hope that your bloodlust can serve as an example for Caiatl. A reminder of how a true warrior acts. You call yourself a Guardian, but we both know the truth: you are a weapon, aimed at a foe of your master's choosing. And if Caiatl lacks the strength to be the master, then she deserves to be the foe.

lines.speaker: Nightmare of Ghaul
lines.text: Caiatl refused to take part in your Hive ritual, did she? At least she maintains some semblance of Cabal pride.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: That pride places us all in jeopardy. She would rather we break than bend with the wind.

lines.speaker: Nightmare of Ghaul
lines.text: As it should be. Better to die true to one's nature than to deny it for the sake of survival.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: Spoken like one who does not know the value of life.

lines.speaker: Calus
lines.text: Humanity and the Cabal, fighting side by side? Aah, daughter, what would the mighty Dominus Ghaul say?

lines.speaker: Nightmare of Ghaul
lines.text: Dead, but not gone. Never gone. In the hearts of our people, I am eternal.

lines.speaker: Nightmare of Ghaul
lines.text: Tell me, Caiatl, are these Guardians not just simple vessels for their Light?

lines.speaker: Caiatl
lines.text: They are more than that. They are born of nothing but ashes, and must rise from them to determine their own destinies by sheer will.

lines.speaker: Nightmare of Ghaul
lines.text: But without the Light... [sighs happily] I have felt them squirm beneath my boot. [chuckles] They are nothing.

lines.speaker: Caiatl
lines.text: And I have felt them at my side, ready to lend their strength if my blade arm tires. Fearless.

lines.speaker: Caiatl
lines.text: Eris Morn... the others do not speak openly of your past.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: Those stories are mine to share.

lines.speaker: Caiatl
lines.text: I know only that you claimed your strength through great hardship... and greater ferocity.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: There was no sacrifice, no bargain or tithe. The only strength I hold is from moving forward when others could not.

lines.speaker: Caiatl
lines.text: There are deep truths within you, witch. Did you... lose your world?

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: I lost so much more than that.

lines.speaker: Calus
lines.text: And do you hear him, too?

lines.speaker: Nightmare of Ghaul
lines.text: She does. And if she is wise, she will listen. End the armistice between humanity and the Cabal. It is an affront against everything that we are.

lines.speaker: Caiatl
lines.text: Zavala. Those instruments you presented to the Crown. What were they?

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: Knitting needles. Do the Cabal not practice a similar craft?

lines.speaker: Caiatl
lines.text: I know what needles are. But what is "knitting"?

lines.speaker: Nightmare of Ghaul
lines.text: Offering the Lightspawn a seat on your council showed weakness, Caiatl. You should have brought them to heel.

lines.speaker: Caiatl
lines.text: As you did? Before they retook their city and you burned in their Traveler's Light?

lines.speaker: Nightmare of Ghaul
lines.text: Ah. So you acted not out of weakness... but out of fear. You cowered before a foe that defeated a greater warrior.

lines.speaker: Caiatl
lines.text: There is a difference between fear and respect. You used to know that.

lines.speaker: Memory of Safiyah
lines.text: Heavy is the burden of leadership, Empress. You see how Zavala strains not to buckle beneath it.

lines.speaker: Caiatl
lines.text: He holds all of humanity on his shoulders.

lines.speaker: Memory of Safiyah
lines.text: And how much do you carry on your own? Rest.

lines.speaker: Caiatl
lines.text: Valus Forge. How fares our defensive perimeter around the Leviathan?

lines.speaker: Lord Saladin
lines.text: The blockade holds. Nothing in, nothing out. Your forces guard the H.E.L.M. as if it were part of their fleet.

lines.speaker: Caiatl
lines.text: You are a member of my War Council. What manner of empire would I lead if your soldiers were not afforded the same protection as my own?

lines.speaker: Lord Saladin
lines.text: An empire doomed to ruin. We stand together, Empress.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: Your Light has guided you back to yourself. You're now both pauper and prince.

lines.speaker: Crow
lines.text: [sighs] It's good to feel... whole again. I just hope Glint gets along with the new me.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: He will understand. A Ghost's bond with their Guardian is a profound thing, not to be taken lightly... or easily forgotten.

lines.speaker: Memory of Safiyah
lines.text: I once said that Lightbearers were more than instruments of violence. But I watch this one work, and I remember that violence can be a useful tool.

lines.speaker: Memory of Uldren
lines.text: You two must be fun at parties.

lines.speaker: Memory of Ghaul
lines.text: The smallest spark can ignite an inferno. The Red Legion might never have come to this system had you stayed away from our forward bases.

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: I knew the Vanguard was risking war with the Cabal when we landed on Mars. But we needed to reach the Black Garden no matter what.

lines.speaker: Memory of Ghaul
lines.text: So you provoked one enemy to avoid annihilation by another. Much like Caiatl when she brought her fleet to Earth.

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: She and I both understand that sometimes, war is the only option. That doesn't make it a good one.

lines.speaker: Memory of Ghaul
lines.text: Even after my death, the remnants of the Red legion fight in my name. They will never bow to Caiatl.

lines.speaker: Lord Saladin
lines.text: That is the power of legacy. The Iron Lords who fought beside me are with me still. I light their braziers every night. So long as I remember them, they are never truly gone. One day, I too will fall, and someone else will tend my flame.

lines.speaker: Memory of Ghaul
lines.text: Well said. May your death be glorious, Saladin Forge.

lines.speaker: Memory of Ghaul
lines.text: I remember Torobatl. How the crowds would take to the streets in celebration of the empire's victories, cheering until the sun rose above the city.

lines.speaker: Caiatl
lines.text: When I close my eyes, I can still see the mountains and the seas, the lush jungles where wild war beasts hunted in packs. That is all gone, now. Likely overrun with Hive chitin and rotten fingus, same as this accursed ship.

lines.speaker: Memory of Ghaul
lines.text: Then keep Torobatl's memory, as you keep mine. And when the time comes... avenge what has been lost.

lines.speaker: Memory of Safiyah
lines.text: Lord Saladin. How long has it been since I first set foot in your camp, my old friend?

lines.speaker: Lord Saladin
lines.text: Longer than I care to recount. I remember how Zavala urged me to turn you away. He didn't think refugees belonged there.

lines.speaker: Memory of Safiyah
lines.text: And you said that if you could not defend the defenseless, then why have a camp at all? It seems he took that to heart, hm?

lines.speaker: Lord Saladin
lines.text: I suppose I taught him well.

lines.speaker: Lord Saladin
lines.text: Zavala. Caiatl told me about Safiyah. Are you all right?

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: Yes... I believe I am. Facing the past wasn't easy, but in the end, it was worth it.

lines.speaker: Lord Saladin
lines.text: The night you returned to the temple, there was... much I left unsaid.

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: You're not to blame, Saladin. I buried my grief, as you did after the Iron Lords fell. We both know better now.

lines.speaker: The Crow
lines.text: For the longest time, I thought I was the only one haunted by my past. Turns out everyone has a skeleton or two in their closet.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: It has always been so. Now that you've learned to see beyond your regrets, perhaps you'll recognize the same pain in others. In time, you will be able to help them as I have. Yours is a compassionate soul, Crow. You have only just begun to discover what you are capable of.

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: I was surprised... to see Ghaul as your friend.

lines.speaker: Caiatl
lines.text: I'm sure he would prefer to be remembered as you knew him: fearsome and terrifying. But I'm happy you saw him as I did: the finest mentor I ever knew.

lines.speaker: Memory of Safiyah
lines.text: Do you remember, Zavala? The night we buried Hakim? The gun in your hand, the moon at your back. And your Ghost...

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: You saved him. Saved him from me.

lines.speaker: Memory of Safiyah
lines.text: You would not have hurt him, Zavala. It would have only been more death.

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: You couldn't have known that. What did you see? A desperate man, dangerous with grief. I would have pulled the trigger.

lines.speaker: Memory of Safiyah
lines.text: What I saw was a broken man, holding a gun to his own heart. He would have sooner killed himself.

lines.speaker: Crow
lines.text: I never thought of Zavala as having a life before the Vanguard.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: He wished it that way. He could not be seen as a father, a husband, or a man. Only as your commander. One of his many sacrifices.

lines.speaker: Calus
lines.text: One by one, I destroyed those who cast me into exile, and yet, my daughter still lives.

lines.speaker: Memory of Ghaul
lines.text: She is quicker than an assassin's blade, and her stomach made of stronger stuff than your poisons. I trained her well.

lines.speaker: Calus
lines.text: Too well. I wonder, sometimes, if I'd promised her to you... would there have ever been a coup? You could have inherited by throne instead of taking it.

lines.speaker: Caiatl
lines.text: Are you sure it's a victory for your Crow to accept his past? Was the Prince of the Awoken not the origin of much suffering for your people?

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: He was. But Crow is still his own person, even if he remembers the burden of his past misdeeds. People can change.

lines.speaker: Caiatl
lines.text: I suppose they can. Perhaps, in that, there is hope for us all.

lines.speaker: Calus
lines.text: How disappointing that Caiatl still fails to see reason. To accept the truth I have offered her. Still, I suppose there is time for her to come around. I am her father, after all.

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: You don't know the first thing about fatherhood.

title: Nightmare Hunt: Fear — Transcript

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: Crota's Brood had an appetite for destruction that knew no bounds. Thus, Phogoth, the Untamed was created. To enact the will of evil upon all. Were he to have succeeded, we might not stand here today. Phogoth is fear incarnate. There's no Nightmare more fitting for the Pyramid to bring forth. And no Nightmare more fitting for you to slaughter.

The Guardian searches for the Nightmore of Phogoth, defeating the Hive which they encounter, including a Nightmare Thrall. A barrier blocking an entrance to the Gatehouse disappears. The Guardian enters the Gatehouse.
The Guardian continues to search for the Nightmare of Phogoth. The Guardian defeats the Hive which they encounter, including several Nightmare Thralls and Nightmare Acolytes.
The Guardian continues to search for the Nightmare of Phogoth. The Guardian defeats the Hive which they encounter, including three Nightmare Thralls.
Nightmare of Phogoth, The Untamed appears.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: That's the Nightmare of Phogoth. Let's get it.
The Guardian defeats Nightmare of Phogoth, The Untamed.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: The Nightmare of Phogoth is no more, Eris.
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

title: Nightmare Hunt: Rage — Transcript

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: The Red Legion arrived and gifted us with a collective pain — the loss of our Light. For a time, all Guardians knew my pain. Too many lost their lives. Those left standing will forever harbor the incurable guilt of survival. I left the City just before the war for reasons of my own. But I harbor that guilt all the same. Even simply a visage of Ghaul is unacceptable. The Pyramid knows this. It feeds off this. Do not let it win.
The Guardian searches for the Nightmare of Dominus Ghaul, defeating the Hive which they encounter, including a Nightmare Acolyte.
The Guardian defeats the Hive, including several Nightmare Thralls, Nightmare Acolytes, and an Ogre.
The Guardian defeats the Cabal, including an Honored Colossus, and heads deeper into the Chamber of Night. The Nightmare of Dominus Ghaul appears.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: We ended Ghaul's reign. His Nightmare stands no chance.
The Guardian defeats the Nightmare of Dominus Ghaul.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: Eris, that's another Nightmare of Ghaul down.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: As long as the Pyramid continues to throw them at us, we will be here to beat them back. Good work.
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

title: Nightmare Hunt: Pride — Transcript

lines.text: The Guardian searches for the Nightmare of Skolas. The Guardian defeats the Hive and the Fallen which are fighting each other, including two Nightmare Shanks. A barrier blocking the entrance to a nearby Fallen Ketch disappears. The Guardian enters the Ketch.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: We are all consumed by that which eats away at us. For Skolas, it was his own hubris. He pursued complete control over all Houses of the Fallen, and through his misguided conquest, many perished. Skolas's memory serves as a permanent reminder of all the lives lost at the whim of a single Kell. No matter how hard the Pyramid may try, we will not cower.

The Guardian heads further into the Ketch, defeating the Fallen and Hive which they encounter, including two Nightmare Shanks. A barrier blocking an entrance disappears. The Guardian continues deeper into the Ketch. Nightmare of Skolas, Kell of Kells appears.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: Skolas Nightmare, dead ahead. It's ours.
The Guardian defeats Nightmare of Skolas, Kell of Kells.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: Eris, Skolas has been taken care of.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: Find me when you are ready.
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

title: Nightmare Hunt: Isolation — Transcript

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: Years ago, Taniks tore the Vanguard apart over a mere bounty. Andal Brask was murdered in cold blood, and the Hunter Vanguard was left without a leader. Taniks would ultimately die for this on the orders of Cayde-6. But the scars he left among all Guardians would never fully heal. Once again, the Pyramid takes advantage of our collective pain. We will not succumb.

The Guardian searches for the Nightmare of Taniks. The Guardian defeats the Hive near the entrance to the Temple of Crota, including two Nightmare Acolytes. A barrier blocking the entrance to the Temple of Crota disappears. The Guardian enters the Temple of Crota.

The Guardian defeats the Hive and the Fallen which they encounter, including two Nightmare Shanks. A barrier blocking an entrance further into the Temple of Crota disappears. The Guardian heads deeper into the Temple of Crota. Nightmare of Taniks, The Scarred appears.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: There's the Nightmare of Taniks. Let's take it down.
The Guardian defeats Nightmare of Taniks, The Scarred.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: Taniks put up a fight. But we got him in the end, Eris.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: Good. We draw closer to the Pyramid with every victory.
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

title: Nightmare Hunt: Servitude — Transcript

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: Zydron. The Vex Gate Lord who denied Guardians access to the Black Garden. The very place from which the Traveler's pain arose. The Pyramid uses Zyrdron's very presence as a reminder of the fear we faced when the Traveler's existence was threatened. Silence his Nightmare.

The Guardian searches for the Nightmare of Zydron. The Guardian defeats the Vex and the Hive which they encounter, including a Nightmare Harpy, several Nightmare Goblins, a Quantum Minotaur, and several Knights. The Guardian enters a cavern with a Vex gate.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: Zydron lost his head to brave Guardians. We'll defeat his Nightmare all the same.
The Nightmare of Zydron, Gate Lord appears. The Guardian defeats the Nightmare of Zydron, Gate Lord.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: Eris, we've put the Nightmare of Zydron to rest.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: The Pyramid's distractions prove weak, time and again. The next time will be no different.
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

title: No One Dreamed it a Trespass — Transcript

lines.speaker: Dialogue Option for the Field Assignment
lines.text: Active Duty patrol received from Toland in Archer's Line

lines.speaker: Toland
lines.text: For millennia, humanity gazed at the Moon and envisioned visiting it. Yet, no one dreamed it a trespass. The Hive is not a welcoming host, as you well know.

lines.speaker: Quest
lines.text: Choir of the Damned, Symphony of Death

title: Of Queens and Worms: Parasitic Pilgrimage — Transcript

lines.text: The Guardian approaches the Court of Thorns with Savathûn’s Worm and the Hive casing from Fynch.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: Mara, are you there? Still nothing.
Savathûn’s Worm: Losing strength. Don’t let me die… will kill you… [screams in pain]

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: [sighs] You’re not going to die. Just… stay with us. Those Hive wells Fynch mentioned must be around here somewhere.
The Guardian searches for the wells.
Savathûn’s Worm: There… ahead. A well…
The Guardian places the worm in the well.
Savathûn’s Worm: Ack! [coughs and retches] Barely! More. Need MORE! Carry me!
Savathûn’s Worm: Need… quick relief… hurry!
The Guardian collects more Hive energy by running through more wells with the Worm.
Savathûn’s Worm: Handle with care! Precious cargo… And they call you a Guardian. [breathes heavily]
Court of Thorns, Savathûn’s Throne World
The Guardian continues to gather Hive energy.
Savathûn’s Worm: [coughing and retching] Any slower, and you might as well take… [grunts] a nap.
The Guardian collections the remaining wells.
Savathûn’s Worm: Only temporary. Deception Queen ran away. No surprise.

lines.speaker: Queen Mara Sov
lines.text: A momentary lapse of judgement, nothing more.

lines.speaker: Queen Mara Sov
lines.text: A story for later. First, we need to ensure the parasite’s stability. Deep in Savathûn’s palace, you’ll find Hive Light.
Savathûn’s Worm: Passageway nearby. Will guide.
Savathûn’s worm guides the Guardian to the Hive Light.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: We’ve got heavy Light readings here.

lines.speaker: Queen Mara Sov
lines.text: Take the Cryptoglyph and fill it with that energy.

lines.speaker: Queen Mara Sov
lines.text: I’m here, in the Throne World, headed to the ritual site. Meet me there once you’ve gathered the energy.
The Guardian grabs the Solar, Arc, and Void Light.
Savathûn’s Worm: Hive don’t suffer thieves. Here they come.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: Now would be a good time for another shortcut, worm!
The Guardian escapes through a portal.
Temple of the Wrathful, Savathûn’s Throne World

lines.speaker: Queen Mara Sov
lines.text: Place the parasite inside the space. Then you must recite the first incantation — oh no.

lines.speaker: Queen Mara Sov
lines.text: The Scorn, many of them. Attracted by the presence of our parasitic friend, no doubt. Start the ritual, now.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: But we don’t know the incantation—
Savathûn’s Worm: I must do everything? Put me down. I’ll recite! Be kind. Keep me alive?
The Guardian places the worm. Scorn enemies spawn and the Guardian defeats them.
If the Guardian leaves Savathûn’s Worm.
Savathûn’s Worm: Ow! Dying here, Guardian! Stay close.
Savathûn’s Worm: Ack! That… really took it… out… of me…

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: Incantation’s complete, but the worm is dying again.
The Guardian picks up the worm.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: Mara, not to be harsh, but what’s going on with you?

lines.speaker: Queen Mara Sov
lines.text: Before coming to you, I sought information about the “Voice in the Dark.'” The Witness. What I found… well… You could say I was granted a personal viewing of our impending doom at the hands of the Witness—its poisons piercing my mind and thoughts. I didn’t know what to do. I had no plan. I was… afraid. I remain haunted, unsure of the next move. But it must be made, regardless.

lines.speaker: Queen Mara Sov
lines.text: Over here. We lack time—the Scorn send their strongest yet. Bring everything to me!

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: Mara, you don’t have to do this. There must be another way.
Mara places the worm inside a gun.
Savathûn’s Worm: Wait, what is this? What have you done?!

lines.speaker: Queen Mara Sov
lines.text: What I said I’d do: provide you with a host. Though I guess this is really more a “prison” of Light.
Savathûn’s Worm: Not what we agreed!

lines.speaker: Queen Mara Sov
lines.text: Enough, worm. You’ll live, just like you wanted. The Scorn—they see the worm as an asset to the Witness. They will not relent until they have it. Take the weapon. Use it against them. I need to finish the ritual, or we risk our parasitic friend escaping.
The Guardian protects Mara while she finishes the ritual.

lines.speaker: Queen Mara Sov
lines.text: Not quite. Our little friend here still owes us information.
Savathûn’s Worm: Me? Make good? After your deception?

lines.speaker: Queen Mara Sov
lines.text: Perhaps you’d prefer my earlier proposition of your insides lining the floor?

Savathûn’s Worm: Always violent. Fine. Have information. But only this. No more. Ever. Truth you seek. Humanity’s Collapse. Even the Witness deceived. The Witch Queen did its bidding. Earned its trust. Rode alongside to apocalypse. Watched many burn. But the Witness turned a violent gaze to Traveler. Witch Queen projected lies. Clever deceptions wrapped in shadow. Tides turned. Witness sent away, back amongst the stars.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: Are you saying Savathûn deceived the Witness? Is she the reason humanity survived?
Savathûn’s Worm: Not the reason. A reason. Not for humanity, but for Traveler. My promise, delivered. Will say no more. Ever.

lines.speaker: Queen Mara Sov
lines.text: Consider the deal upheld. This is exactly what we sought. For now, I have one final task for you—the weapon. Keep it safe and secret. We can’t afford anyone else getting their hands on the information it holds. I must leave. Parasite, it’s been… uh…
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

title: Country Radio I: Amanda and Crow — Transcript

lines.speaker: The Crow
lines.text: Amanda. I need to talk to you.

lines.speaker: Holliday
lines.text: Don't talk to me like that. [sighs] Look, I know you're sorry. I know it wasn't really "you." I wanna forgive you. I really do. I… I tried to pull Crow and Uldren Sov apart.

lines.speaker: The Crow
lines.text: I tried too. But it wasn't right.

lines.speaker: Holliday
lines.text: I wish I could see you another way, but… I don't. I—I can't. Not yet.

lines.speaker: The Crow
lines.text: Tell me what to do, and I’ll do it.

lines.speaker: Holliday
lines.text: It's not like that. [sighs] I know it ain't fair to you. And maybe I'll feel different someday. But not now.

lines.speaker: Holliday
lines.text: There's tough times ahead of us—we gotta work together. It's like y'all's Ghosts always say… Eyes up, Guardian.

title: No Time Left — Transcript

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: Calus encroaches upon the Veil. The activation of the Radial Mast is imminent.

lines.speaker: Rohan
lines.text: If the Veil is compromised, Neomuna will fall. Then all of Sol will follow.

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: Strand will be our edge against Calus. The Guardian is ready to wield it… I think.

lines.speaker: Nimbus
lines.text: Rohan and I are with you. This is OUR city!

lines.speaker: Caiatl
lines.text: The Shadow Legion are honorless cowards. They shall share Calus's grave.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: It's that suppression field again! We can't use all of our power!

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: Go closer to it. I have a hypothesis.

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: That device is of Pyramid origin, built to suppress our powers—our KNOWN powers. Calus is not prepared for Strand. Use it to overcome their suppression fields!

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: Scanning the area for Strand now!

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: Your Strand readings are higher than they've ever been!

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: Your training's prepared you for this. Strand flows through you, as it flows through everything.

lines.speaker: Nimbus
lines.text: Hey, Guardian? I got my hands on some schematics for Terran toys. Thought I'd put the replicator to good use.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: The landing zone's clear! What were these, uh, "Terran toys" you mentioned?

lines.speaker: Nimbus
lines.text: Something called a "Drake Tank." Looks like fun.

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: You stole those schematics from my files, didn't you?

lines.speaker: Nimbus
lines.text: The Cabal have me pinned down!

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: This Shadow Legion position is heavily fortified. We're blocked as well.

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: Take out their fuel cells and clear a path to the Radial Mast.

lines.speaker: Rohan
lines.text: I'm counting on you, Guardian. I'll need backup with Nimbus out of the fight.

lines.speaker: Caiatl
lines.text: We're holding the skies and keeping Calus's reinforcements at bay for now, but it won't hold forever.

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: Rohan and the Guardian are on the way.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: Their suppression fields even disable the tanks! Calus was really prepared for us. But not prepared enough! I'm running another scan for Strand.

lines.speaker: Rohan
lines.text: I'm getting delayed! How close are you to the Radial Mast?

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: Remember, the Radial Mast must be stopped before it forges a connection with the Veil!
