lines.text: You see what was done! Our Ether tanks, smashed! Our supplies, stolen! Our home, defaced!
Saint-14 looks towards the destroyed supplies.

lines.speaker: Lakshmi-2
lines.text: This is not surprising. The locals have been under enormous pressure. You are lucky it was not worse.

lines.speaker: Mithrax
lines.text: This destruction helps no one but the Vex. Please, instead of teaching your people to fear us, tell them the truth.

lines.speaker: Lakshmi-2
lines.text: The truth is that your kind preyed upon us for as long as we can remember. There is nothing I can say that will make them forget.

lines.speaker: Mithrax
lines.text: House Light has never raised arms against humanity!

lines.speaker: Lakshmi-2
lines.text: Your Houses and titles are layers of politics. You are still Fallen.

lines.speaker: Lakshmi-2
lines.text: And you've had it! We allowed your brood to squat and chitter here in our city, but still the Vex simulation persists! If you are displeased with how you have been treated for your failure, then I suggest you camp elsewhere.

lines.speaker: Mithrax
lines.text: Your people destroyed what little we possessed. Now we have nothing, nowhere to go.

lines.speaker: Lakshmi-2
lines.text: Humanity faced a challenge like that once.

lines.speaker: Lakshmi-2
lines.text: We banded together and built a city with walls to keep our enemies outside… where they belong.
Lakshmi-2 turns and transmats out of the area. Saint-14 turns away from Mithrax just as Mithrax turns toward Saint-14.

lines.speaker: Mithrax
lines.text: We hear her broadcasts, but more than that — we feel the energy of her words in the air. Sharp as blades pointed at an enemy. At us.

lines.speaker: Saint-14
lines.text: You cannot ask people to live alongside their monsters.

lines.speaker: Mithrax
lines.text: Listen to me now, Saint. Let me tell you something about monsters.
Mithrax explains how the Eliksni view Saint-14.

lines.speaker: Mithrax
lines.text: Once, in a city grander even than yours, we prospered. But it did not last. Our Great Machine abandoned us. And when we pursued it… you sent something back. A creature fueled by hatred… It tore through our great houses like they were nothing. And then it came for the rest of us. Nowhere was safe from its insatiable rage. In its eyes, even the most innocent of Eliksni were still Fallen. It could die, but it would not stay dead. It would shake off the rot and rise again. And if it caught you in its crushing embrace, impaled you on its ragged crest, dragged you screaming into its foul shell… none lived to speak of these horrors. It called itself… the Saint. My people must now see the creature every day. It sees us. If we wish to survive, we must all learn… to live alongside our monsters.
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

title: Path of the Splicer III: Speak with Mithrax — Transcript

lines.text: The Guardian returns to the Eliksni Wing and approaches the Splicer Servitor after defeating Fantis, Oppressive Mind.

lines.speaker: Mithrax
lines.text: Your powers grow to fight the Vex, but still their offense increases. We Sacred Splicers study the Vex. We learn to move through them like tall grass. But these, they are strange to me. Their focus is unpredictable. This frustrates me… I can see the data streams as you walk through their space, but I cannot see from where they flow. It is as though a fog pushes in from cold water… it could be the soft voice of my doubt, here in this false night. But it could be something greater, something no Splicer has encountered before. You must continue to enter their network; destroy what you find inside. Each victory cuts one of the threads that hold this Endless Night in place. The Vex will send powerful foes against you, but be not swayed. Keep to the path.
Splicer Servitor — Path of the Splicer III
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

title: Path of the Splicer IV: Broadcast from Lakshmi-2 — Transcript

lines.text: The Guardian listens to a broadcast from Lakshmi-2

lines.speaker: Lakshmi-2
lines.text: People of the Last City: The Vanguard protects us from enemies outside our walls. But did you know they also protect us from information? Did you know that the Fallen unleashed the Vex on Europa? That they corrupt our Guardians with the poisoned gift of Stasis, tempting them to wield the Darkness? These same Fallen are now inside our city, at the invitation of the Vanguard. Ikora Rey knows all this and more. Her Hidden spies report as much. Yet she continues to support these false alliances over her own people! Whether her lies are born of malice or incompetence matters not. What matters is that I have gazed into the future and foreseen bodies in our streets. Make no mistake: an invasion is coming. And if we are to triumph, we must first take back our city.

title: Path of the Splicer IV: Speak with Ikora Rey — Transcript

lines.text: The Tower, The Last City, Earth
The Guardian approaches Ikora Rey in the Tower's Bazaar, after defeating Dikast, Oppressive Mind.

lines.speaker: Ikora Rey
lines.text: There's been a disturbance: sabotage in the Eliksni camp. This wasn't just an attack on their Ether stores; someone wanted to send a message. Our citizens forget who they were before they found the safety of the City's walls. It's easy to mistake change as the frontline of a battlefield, but this is a time for level heads and compassion. Saint-14 is already en route to investigate. I trust him, but he is torn between duty and doubt. And Lakshmi… The Vanguard has tolerated her broadcasts, as Zavala doesn't believe it's our place to interfere in civilian politics. I see now that was a mistake. We can't allow anyone to jeopardize our alliance with the House of Light, no matter their motives. Our citizens must see that the Eliksni are people, just like them. Get down there. Be the calm the City needs. Hear out grievances and keep tensions low while I root out the perpetrators. It's time that Lakshmi and I had a little talk.
Ikora Rey — Path of the Splicer IV
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

lines.speaker: Path of the Splicer V
lines.text: Broadcast from Mithrax and Ikora Rey

title: Path of the Splicer IV: Mission Briefing — Transcript

lines.text: The Guardian approaches the Splicer Servitor in the Eliksni Wing.

lines.speaker: Mithrax
lines.text: The path leads you to me once more, Guardian. This Endless Night presses down on us all. I hear the City groan with the strain. The dark brings sickness now. Few can find sleep. The people hear of your triumphs against the Vex, but they see only dark skies above. They are being bent… and some may break. I will aid if I can. I will not be proud, but let the citizens see that we are suffering with them. I have faith they will see us for who we are. The Light always shines through in the end. But for now, the work must begin again. Go.
Splicer Servitor — Path of the Splicer IV
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

title: Path of the Splicer IV: Speak with Mithrax — Transcript

lines.text: The Guardian approaches the Splicer Servitor in the Eliksni Wing after speaking with Lakshmi-2 regarding the sabotage at the Eliksni camp.

lines.speaker: Mithrax
lines.text: I have no words left to speak. Lakshmi-2, the Saint… I do not know if I reached them. In truth, I do not know if I even reach you… Hm. Ah, the darkness of this night weighs on me more than any other. Know this: I will not stop fighting for those in this city — even those who did this. The Light passes through us all… we focus it through the prism of our will. Those who attacked us were blinded by fear, poisoned by venomous words — They were focused badly. Bent badly. But they are not truly our enemies. We will not seek vengeance — we are not the monsters some believe us to be. Walking the path of the Light takes strength. That is what we will remember tonight as fear and hunger gnaw at us. As our hatchlings sleep in ashes.
Splicer Servitor — Path of the Splicer IV
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

lines.speaker: Path of the Splicer V
lines.text: Broadcast from Mithrax and Ikora Rey

title: Path of the Splicer IV: Transmission from Lakshmi-2 — Transcript

lines.text: The Guardian approaches the holoprojector in the Eliksni Wing, and receives a secure communication from Lakshmi-2 after the sabotage at the Eliksni camp.

lines.speaker: Lakshmi-2
lines.text: Guardian. I regret you had to witness my outburst earlier, with the Fallen leader. I am not a diplomat, and sometimes, I can be… terse. I know terrible things have been done in the name of the City. In the name of the Future War Cult. In my name. You understand, though. The City is a living thing, and it is rejecting the Fallen like a fever burning out an infection. I will speak to the Fallen leader. Tell it that the Future War Cult will personally replenish their supplies when they are ready to move on. I do not wish them to think badly of us. I know they are your associates. What a City we would have if everyone's heart was as big as yours! Have you heard the song of the people echoing through the City? "Rise up as one, march towards the sun…" Hmm. The words of people reaching for dawn in this Endless Night. People who have still not given up hope. Neither have I. And if you were wondering… this was not the conflict I have foreseen. No. That will come later… unless I can stop it.
Splicer Servitor — Path of the Splicer IV
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

lines.speaker: Path of the Splicer V
lines.text: Broadcast from Mithrax and Ikora Rey

lines.speaker: Quest
lines.text: Blood in the Garden, Not Forged In Light

title: Path of the Splicer V: Broadcast from Mithrax and Ikora Rey — Transcript

lines.text: The Guardian listens to a broadcast from Mithrax and Ikora Rey.

lines.speaker: Mithrax
lines.text: Eliksni of the House Light, hear Misraaks now. I know many of you feared this place. You have seen death at the hands of the Guardians — it was right to expect death in their house. But I said, and say again, that if we help them, they will help us. And here we are, alive. It is true that some have attacked our new home. It is true that some try to share their hate with us. It is always so. But if Eliksni feel Darkness inside, only look up to see the Great Machine, and know that House of Light is blessed.

lines.speaker: Ikora
lines.text: We're all blessed to have such friends in dark times. Humanity will not allow these hateful and ignorant acts to define us. We will prove it by bringing those responsible to justice.

lines.speaker: Mithrax
lines.text: Walk the path of hardship with joy in your hearts. Be brave.

title: Path of the Splicer V: Mission Briefing — Transcript

lines.text: The Guardian approaches the Splicer Servitor in the Eliksni Wing.

lines.speaker: Mithrax
lines.text: I greet you in the Light, my friend. There have been no more attacks from inside the walls. I spoke my heart-words to all who would hear: we have no anger within us. We will not be led to violence, no matter how wide the path. We now must focus on the Vex. The machines do not stop to consider our situation, and neither should you. I can still improve your Gauntlet, and your Splicer training must continue. Do not waste your energies on us. My Eliksni have been through much, but cruel words and thoughtless deeds will not break us. Let us continue our work.
Splicer Servitor — Path of the Splicer V
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

lines.speaker: Path of the Splicer V
lines.text: Broadcast from Mithrax and Ikora Rey

lines.speaker: Path of the Splicer V
lines.text: Broadcast from Mithrax and Ikora Rey

title: Path of the Splicer V: Speak with Mithrax — Transcript

lines.text: The Guardian approaches the Splicer Servitor in the Eliksni Wing after speaking with Saint-14.

lines.speaker: Mithrax
lines.text: I see you have overcome the Vex again. We are both doing what we must. I have not spoken with the Saint, but I believe hearing my story softened him somehow. I saw one of our young run across his path. The Saint raised a hand in greeting, and the hatchling recoiled and fled. The Saint watched it run — the reaction seemed to wound him. I will reach out to this child. She acted out of fear and was unkind. She should know the image of the Saint we use to chase evil is only a story. If we are to survive this long night, we must be able to see one another as what we truly are.
Splicer Servitor — Path of the Splicer V
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

title: Path of the Splicer V: Speak with Saint-14 — Transcript

lines.text: The Tower, The Last City, Earth
The Guardian approaches Saint-14 in the Tower's Hangar after defeating Dimio, Oppressive Mind.

lines.speaker: Saint-14
lines.text: I have thought much on Mithrax's story. We do monstrous things to fight monsters. It seemed simple then. When the City first formed, Titans were the walls. We did not think of our enemies when we fought. We thought only of protecting our people. Survival until the next day, no matter how. To be seen as… as a terror. A destroyer. To know children tremble in fear at my name, and mourn what I have taken from them. This is not the Saint-14 I know. I can never forgive what the Old Houses did to us, but these are not the old Houses. They are dead. What do we gain from more death? This… lashing out against defenseless people. It is the act of a coward. Mithrax risked much to trust us. If his House of Light can forgive… perhaps we must try to see the Fallen — Eliksni — as they see themselves… or none of us will ever be anything but monsters. We must be more than the enemies of our enemies.
Saint-14 — Path of the Splicer V
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

title: Patrols: Derelict Leviathan — Transcript

lines.text: The Guardian interacts with their first patrol beacon.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: These Nightmares have been drawn from the Moon by the Leviathan's siren song. The trauma that bore them into this world is anchored there, not here. They are lost. Perhaps even... confused, if such phantoms can experience emotion beyond the snapshot of pain they represent. We may be able to disperse them by resolving their associated traumas.
The Guardian interacts with a Salvage patrol beacon.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: Abandoned and alone on the cold and lifeless Moon, this Nightmare recalls the feeling of being separated from something precious. We may be able to substitute a replacement.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: This Nightmare is born from an emotion of desperation and loss, and we may be able to dispel it by providing it with a substantial offering.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: Loss and longing turned to desperation and panic. We will need to provide an offering to this Nightmare in order to provide it the desired catharsis.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: Only an offering made in good faith will disperse this Nightmare, and its needs seem... specific. I believe I know where we could find a suitable substitution.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: I have identified an offering that may have this Nightmare disperse. I have transmitted the telemetry to your Ghost.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: This Nightmare is lost here, an echo of Moon-born trauma. If we provide it with a suitable offering, it will find catharsis, and sublimate into the dark.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: Like the ghost stories of old, this Nightmare haunts the Leviathan with unresolved affairs. If we provide it with a specific material offering, it may yet disperse.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: In order to disperse this Nightmare, we must find an offering to satiate its imprinted desire. I believe I have identified something that may serve our purposes.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: A material offering should provide this Nightmare with enough cognitive dissonance that it simply... ceases to be. It is the best we can hope for.
The Guardian interacts with a Combat patrol beacon.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: We must find a suitable offering from among the resonant materials of the Leviathan. That should cause this Nightmare to disperse.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: This Nightmare relives the trauma of a Guardian long since dead. Only violence will bring it the catharsis it yearns for.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: This Nightmare suffers in endless death at the hands of the Hive God Crota. Only further violence will lessen its pain.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: I feel this Nightmare's agony and terror, a moment of death stretched across time. It will only be released by more violence... on another.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: This Nightmare is a snapshot of suffering, and only through inflicting more pain can we banish it from the Leviathan.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: A Guardian's fear of final death burned this Nightmare into the fabric of space. Now all it knows — all it will be satisfied by — is more pain.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: A Nightmare, drawn to the Leviathan, seeking the death of faceless enemies as a catharsis for its own suffering. It asks you to deliver such violence.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: So much pain, so much suffering. And yet it will only languish here unless we deliver its pain onto others. Such is the cycle.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: I feel this Guardian's pain so clearly. The taste of bile in my mouth, the blind hunger for revenge. They want blood.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: Fear of death compounding into resentment and hate of the living. This Nightmare desires death for others, and it will only fade if you deliver it.

title: Payback — Transcript

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: Guardian, you've got a tough road ahead. So, I'm sending in Holliday with something… special.

lines.speaker: Cayde
lines.text: Are we talking Gjallahorn special? Or an Ikora philosophy lesson special?

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: Just keep moving. Storm the facility and board that Cabal Carrier. No matter the cost — we MUST get to the Almighty.

lines.speaker: Cayde
lines.text: So, Zavala, I gotta ask you something. When you told our Guardian friend here, and I quote, "I need Cayde," did you by any chance happen to maybe… cry?

lines.speaker: Cayde
lines.text: Let the record show; no denial.

lines.speaker: Amanda
lines.text: Still a couple clicks out, Commander. This girl's heavy.

lines.speaker: Cayde
lines.text: You got them a tank? How come I never got a tank?

lines.speaker: Amanda
lines.text: You know you'd just break it.
The guardian starts fighting their way through the Cabal base.

lines.speaker: Amanda
lines.text: Guardian, holler my way if you need another one of those armored beauties. Plenty more where that came from.

lines.speaker: Cayde
lines.text: Oh, so I get nothing, and they get as many as they want. I see how it is.
A blast door blocks the way.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: We should find the controls for that blast door. They're around here somewhere.

lines.speaker: Amanda
lines.text: Heads up! That carrier's spinning up its engines. You might want to pick up the pace!

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: Thumos is on that carrier. He has what you need to infiltrate the Almighty. MOVE!
A Cabal tank gets air lifted in.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: Of course the Red Legion have tanks too.
The Guardian defeats the Cabal tank

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: Well, they've retracted the bridge. We're not going to be able to cross that gap.

lines.speaker: Cayde
lines.text: Oh, your super tank cant fly? Oh…
The Guardian finds an access terminal to extend the bridge

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: That should give us a way across.

lines.speaker: Cayde
lines.text: So, if it wasn't to give me a tank, why did you send our favourite guardian to find me?

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: Your… high-risk, high-reward combat manoeuvres can be effective and… inspirational.

lines.speaker: Cayde
lines.text: Well, yeah, but with a tank, they could be like a million times MORE inspirational.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: We're almost out of the tunnels and coming up on the carrier.

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: Good. The only thing standing between you and the Almighty is Thumos, the Unbroken. He's a Blood Guard. One of Ghaul's "chosen". The Red Legion will die for him. Why don't you help them with that?

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: Wait… see those generators? We need to take them out if we're going to board that carrier.
The Guardian destroys the first generator
The Guardian destroys the second generator.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: Shield's down, but the ship's about to launch without us!

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: Keep that carrier on the ground!

lines.speaker: Cayde
lines.text: Couple missiles up its tailpipe ought to do the job.
The Guardian shoots the carriers tail pipe

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: The carrier's grounded. Now lets find Thumos.

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: Good work Guardian. And Cayde… after this is over, I'll talk to Holliday about your tank.

lines.speaker: Cayde
lines.text: Aw. I missed you too, buddy.
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

lines.speaker: Path of the Splicer V
lines.text: Broadcast from Mithrax and Ikora Rey

title: Pilgrimage: Garden of Esila, Dead Tree — Transcript

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: You Guardians embrace death. But, it is not final for you, and so it has no weight, no impact. The Awoken believe in its finality. We believe we are charting toward a final future, a final shape. It is our duty to help shape it before we are gone.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: We Awoken have one foot in the Darkness and one in the Light. Your Traveler is a gardener, so we garden, too. But the Darkness demands each thing fit to its final shape - and so we accept when something must die.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: Let this tree serve as a reminder that all things have their end. There is a certain amount of time that every one of us is granted. We must all make the most of it.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: The Hive preach the gospel of the final shape: death. In our way, we believe in its power, too - but the Hive have such limited imagination. They have not heard the song of the Sky. There are more ways to carve and craft than cutting and killing.
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

title: Pilgrimage — Transcript

lines.text: The Guardian approaches a door. A Hive Knight charges toward the Guardian. Ana Bray shoots the Knight from behind, killing it.

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: Well, there were a lot of them. But you did great.

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: Come on, let's see what's hiding in here! Besides hordes and hordes of frozen Hive, I mean.
Ghost and Guardian turn to nod at each other.

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: You two clear a path while I try to find a way into Clovis Bray.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: We've encountered Warminds before, but Ikora said Rasputin was trapped on Earth.

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: Rasputin is capable of operating across multiple systems simultaneously.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: So all those times the Vanguard was trying to talk to him in the Cosmodrome…

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: They were engaging fragments of Rasputin left behind after the Collapse. But his core mind was always here.
Guardian clears area of Cabal forces and then approaches a console. Ana Bray appears.

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: I'm here. I'm really here. I can't believe it. Clovis Bray. I'm… home.

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: The main access is encrypted. Good thing I know a few tricks. At least that seems to run in the family.

lines.speaker: Concierge AI
lines.text: Personnel Identified: Dr. Anastasia Bray. Welcome to the Clovis Bray Research facility, the fabled "Cradle of Invention," on Mars. You are part of an important moment in history. Together, we will strive to reach beyond the stars. Remember, you are Clovis Bray.
The Guardian walks through a doorway leading further into the Clovis Bray facility.

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: Looks like Rasputin's core is housed in a separate structure. Hope you're up for a little exploring.
The Guardian ventures further into the Clovis Bray facility.

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: The Brays dreamed big. I don't know much about my family, but I know that.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: I'm picking up a lot of Hive activity. They're swarming the core.

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: On it. Let me try to access the security systems.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: What's the status on the security systems?

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: I'm working on it. Hang in there.
The Guardian continues towards Rasputin's mind core.

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: Come on, Rasputin. Give me something here!
The Valkyrie appears, killing a group of Hive from above.

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: It's the Valkyrie. Rasputin's weapon. I think… he heard us.
The Guardian defeats Ekdala Xolborne and Dultur Xolborne. A door opens.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: Ana? The door's unlocked. Did you…?

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: It wasn't me. Maybe he's inviting us inside. Maybe this is where questions finally turn into answers.
Ana, the Guardian, and Ghost approach the next door. The door opens, revealing Zavala.

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: What do you think you're doing? Do you have any idea how dangerous this thing is?!

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: What were you trying to do to Rasputin?

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: Rasputin is Vanguard business, Anastasia. Not yours. You do not belong here.

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: You belonged in the City! But instead of standing by your brothers and sisters when Ghaul came for us, you were here, doing what you always do - what you were never supposed to do.

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: I did what I believed to be right. I came here to protect Humanity. Isn't that what Guardians are supposed to do? This is a war of many fronts. And there's more than one way to fight it, Zavala. Look, you tried to shield the entire world, but you can't. There's got to be a better way.

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: And you think Rasputin is the answer? It's gone silent. It's a broken weapon. Too dangerous to be left alone, and too unpredictable to wield.

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: That might be true. Or maybe he has nothing to say. Maybe, just maybe, we never bothered to ask him what he wanted.

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: I don't have time to go through this with you again. You had no right…

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: I have every right. You don't understand the connection I share with Rasputin. Here, let me show you.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: OK, we should really figure out exactly what's doing that.

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: I can tell you. Rasputin was not the only thing to awaken on Mars.

lines.speaker: Ana Bray
lines.text: I thought we were done for. And then Rasputin... I didn't know if he would answer. I mean, I hoped he would. But you never know with him. That javelin, though, wow, that's one hell of a confirmation. But the REAL problem is Xol. The Hive became what they are today by making dark pacts with worm gods. Xol is one of those gods. I've been talking to Zavala and he has an idea. Something that Xol won't be able to resist. Problem is? That something is in the EDZ and everyone wants it.
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

title: Pilgrimage: Garden of Esila, Garden Bench — Transcript

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: My friends and I used to come here. Now they are dead. Whatever rituals you enjoy, Guardian, whatever little things you hold dear - cling to them while you have them. You don't know when they'll disappear.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: I used to come to this bench and sit with Nascia. She and I entered the coven at the same time. She bonded to her Harbinger before I did - I was so jealous, and I could not say so, because we were taught to feel no jealousy. Not all lessons stick.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: Before the Battle of Saturn, there were seven of us. It is good to be myself again, good to be whole - but I miss the afternoons where my friends and I would come to these benches to talk and enjoy the sun.
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

title: Pilgrimage: Garden of Esila, Queensfoil — Transcript

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: Queensfoil. Orin the Lost stole several of these plants before she embarked on her fool's journey into the heliopause. I tried to warn her, but her curiosity was overwhelming. She did not listen to me.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: See that plant? It's queensfoil. The leaves, carefully prepared, can be used to see into other planes, other realms — but the power of the vision can destroy the weak.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: That’s queensfoil. It’s highly poisonous, but when the leaves are properly dried and crushed, it can be used to induce prophecy. The risks are immeasurable.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: When my friend Nascia was still in training to become a Techeun, she dried her own queensfoil and tried to induce a vision. It nearly killed her. Give that plant a wide berth.
Discuss this Transcript on our forum
Invitation of the Nine - Mystery and Potential (Visit 9)

title: Pilgrimage: Garden of Esila, Techeun Statues — Transcript

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: Those statues there… look up at them. Those Techeuns died a vicious irreversible death. They died in trance, each one screaming with the others voice, each one unable to comprehend the horror of the thing that had killed them.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: The Techeuns you see here died while they were in trance together. Sometimes when you are in communion you cannot see what is coming close, like the Aphelion. Their last words were these "First it shimmered… then it crawled… then it screamed."

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: These three Techeuns were victim to the Aphelion. I pray you never see it my friend, because no matter what gods you have killed, you will not survive it.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: We Techeuns are taught absolute obedience to our Queen. We have no desires but what our Queen desires, we have no fears but what our Queen fears. Good traits. But weaknesses against certain enemies. Like the Taken. Like the Aphelion.

title: Pilgrimage: Garden of Esila, View — Transcript

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: When Mara and Illyn began to shape the Dreaming City, this was where they started. They stood on the edge of the world with rough rocks all around, and they saw the potential of what this place could be.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: Turn and look out over the clouds. Breathe in… then out… Now turn. Look at the gardens. Study them. Take them in. Everything you see is the reason we're here, Guardian. If beautiful places like this cannot survive, then why fight at all?

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: When the Awoken first arrived in the Reef, Mara was not our Queen. She was simply our leader. We MADE HER our Queen. This is where she was crowned. This is where we knelt and pledged our devotion to her.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: Your Traveler terraformed your planets. But the Awoken terraformed the Dreaming City. It is our creation. It is a reflection of our people - not a false gift from a skittish god.
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

title: Pilgrimage: Garden of Esila, Tree — Transcript

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: Dozens of good people died walking over these cliffs. They were lured to their death by an Ahamkara during a celebration of the solstice. Those creatures… They can turn on you in an instant if you aren't wary.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: This was the site of a mass murder. An Ahamkara of immense power tricked dozens of civilians into walking right off the edge of these cliffs. We saved none of them. And to our great shame, the Ahamkara - Azirim, he was called - escaped.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: Step past the tree. Peek down over the ledge. That drop goes on for some time. Now imagine a voice whispering to you, luring you, promising you that your feet will find solid ground where, in truth, there is only air… Ahamkara lies.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: A great tragedy once occurred at these cliffs. It was early in our relationship with the Ahamkara, before we'd learned their tricks, before we'd learned how best to live alongside them without becoming their prey…
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

title: Pilgrimage: Gardens of Esila, Bridge — Transcript

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: These gardens were named for Esila, a famed poet and storyteller who chronicled our history and sang our epics. She was one of the first to stand in support of Mara during the Reckoning.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: Do you see the arches before you? We call it a cleft gate. The architecture symbolizes the divide between the past we left behind and the present we live in now. There is no bridge between them because there is no going back.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: Look into the sky. See that portal? It controls access to the Tangled Shore - and crucially, it holds the cloaking technology that we use to disguise and protect the Dreaming City.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: There is a large gazebo just beyond this bridge. It was Queen Mara's favourite place to meditate, to think. When we first realised that Oryx was on his way into our system - that is where we found her when we delivered the news.
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

title: Pilgrimage: Harbinger’s Seclude, Eao’s Nest — Transcript

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: This bowl was once a nest for Eao - he was a sly little Ahamkara, always laughing, always twining around your legs, whispering lies, saying, "I have seen your eyes, o witch-mage mine." We never expected him to go bad.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: This was once a resting place for an Ahamkara who loved stories. He would recite all of our myths, name all our heroes… And that's where we went wrong. We should have never trusted him to keep our secrets.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: This little chamber was once a home for an Ahamkara who betrayed the Awoken. He crept out of the Dreaming City and went to whisper in the ears of Warlocks who wondered who we were - and so we had to kill him. The Warlocks, too.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: Ah… This is where Eao liked to rest, before Sjur hunted him down and skewered him for his deceit. One of your Warlocks bartered for his corpse and traded away his bones. Another mistake. You must never scatter the bones.
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

title: Pilgrimage: Harbinger’s Seclude, Alis Li — Transcript

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: That is a statue of Alis Li, the great bargainer. They say she turned the Green into the storm. They say she cast out the lightning sails to attract both the Light and the Dark. But those are not my stories to tell. Not really…

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: Alis Li, the very first of our queens. She was given a precious opportunity to build a society in the way she thought best. She chose equality, exploration, engineering, peace… and her wisdom led us to paradise.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: Alis Li. I did not know her; I was not born in the Distributary - but Mara knew her. Illyn knew her. Uldren, too. They all spoke highly of Alis. She was an excellent starship pilot and a levelheaded ruler. A good queen.
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

title: Pilgrimage: Harbinger’s Seclude, Cliffs — Transcript

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: The Dreaming City is built upon a disc that contains a silver sea. The water is real, but the horizon is an illusion if you're accustomed to spherical worlds. If you went far enough, you'd fall off the edge of the disc.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: There is a stabilization ring beyond the horizon that holds the City in alignment. When water goes spilling off the horizon, it is captured and fed back into the atmosphere before it dissipates into space.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: When we helped Queen Mara build this place, she felt it was essential to incorporate water into the landscape - to honor our old home in the Distributary, to make everything here feel more… real.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: This waterfall is not fed by a river. Instead, its water comes from hydrocapture systems buried deep in the bedrock. We recycle all of our water - the whole place runs on a closed ecosystem.
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

title: Pilgrimage: Harbinger's Seclude, Devna Tel — Transcript

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: Queen Deva Tel and her loyal Techeuns. Devna's rule predates the arrival of the Awoken in the Reef, as did all that came before Queen Mara. We built these statues in their memory.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: These statues depict Queen Devna Tel and her Techeuns, Yara and Imar. Imar is himself noteworthy, as he was a man. There are no prohibitions against men becoming Techeuns - nor against men ruling. It's simply rare.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: This is a statue of Queen Devna Tel, ruler of the Distributary, last of her name. She held the throne when the Sky and the Deep came to the Awoken to collect their terms. She chose to stay, and Mara chose to go.
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

title: Pilgrimage: Harbinger’s Seclude, Flowers — Transcript

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: Pink asphodelia is grown only in the Dreaming City, and we do not pick the flowers except to celebrate a birth or mourn a death. They have a unique power over the Awoken soul.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: Asphodelia flowers are taboo to pick except under special circumstances. Getting a thorn lodged in your skin causes paranoia, madness, violence… but the petals themselves, steeped in tea, bring peace and enlightenment.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: Asphodelia… The flowers are a symbol of the fragility of life, and they were originally planted from clippings gathered in a place of enduring death.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: Pink asphodelia. It's a cultivated strain said to descend from the flowers in Black Garden. Among our people, Prince Uldren was the first to walk the Garden, and the first to bring these back.
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

title: Pilgrimage: Harbinger’s Seclude, Meeting Pillar — Transcript

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: The Awoken knew the Ahamkara long before the Guardians ever noticed them. We made our alliances and cut our deals at this pillar - and for the most part, we lived alongside each other.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: Dozens of Ahamkara have crawled or flown or slithered across this platform since it was built. They had the power to change their shape, to reform themselves to match the expectation of their beholders. We expected nothing of them, and so they came as they were.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: It was here that we first struck an agreement with the Ahamkara and here that we met the very last of them. Those creatures have keen memories, and they love patterns and ceremony. When you start a tradition with them, they follow it through.
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

title: Pilgrimage: Harbinger’s Seclude, Elevator — Transcript

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: Turn. Look down. You stand above the entrance to the Hall of Names. Techeuns and Paladins alike used to receive their titles in that Hall, witnessed by the living and the lost alike.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: Turn and look behind you. Do you see the two statues? The left hand is for creation. The right is for destruction. Illyn used to say that we can hold fate in just one hand at a time.
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

title: Pilgrimage: Harbinger’s Seclude, Kelda Wadj — Transcript

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: When a Techeun takes her title, she must swear a sacred oath to cover her eyes for the remainder of her life, showing them to no one - not even those closest to her. They can only be uncovered again when she has died.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: That statue depicts Kelda Wadj. She was Illyn's mentor in the Distributary. For all her wisdom, I'm told she was one of the loudest voices to speak out against Queen Mara's decision to leave.
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

title: Pilgrimage: Harbingers Seclude, Shiny Geode — Transcript

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: I have heard it said that the Awoken brought the Ahamkara into this system — that we found them in the ruins of the planet that we carved into the base of the Dreaming City — but if you ask me, they came from the Nine.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: The Ahamkara always came and went from the Dreaming City by way of this platform, which meant they always passed by these geodes. We used them as protective measures. Shiny surfaces can reveal some of the Ahamkara's secrets — if you know what to look for.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: Reflections are powerful things. They can disarm certain kinds of magic. Wish-magic, in particular, is susceptible — since it is so heavily dependent on expectation and perception…

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: Know this, Guardian. If an Ahamkara has hidden itself away beyond Jupiter, if the last of them did not die here in the Dreaming City… you can reveal their true intentions with reflective surfaces.
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

title: Pilgrimage: Harbinger’s Seclude, Shrine — Transcript

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: We call this the Hall of Names. It was once a place of ceremony. Young women - and sometimes men - came here to be transformed as a final rite of passage in becoming a Techeun.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: Look at all the statues around you. How many queens? How many Techeuns came before you? The Dreaming City is older than your Tower, your Last City - but the carvings here almost all honor people that never once stepped foot in the Reef.
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

title: Pilgrimage: Harbinger’s Seclude, Osana Sov — Transcript

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: Osana Sov. She does not deserve the respect my lady grants her with that statue. Uldren argued against putting it up; he thought Osana should be forgotten. But Queen Mara chose to remember.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: That statue depicts Osana Sov - mother to Queen Mara and Prince Uldren. Though she is venerated here as a queen, she was not royal herself. The Awoken do not believe in royal lines or inheritance.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: You can tell a statue of a queen from a statue of a Techeun by what they hold in their hands. The queens hold nothing at all. Techeuns hold symbols of life - orbs, lights…
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

title: Pilgrimage: Spine of Keres, Cave — Transcript

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: I don't know who or what that face depicts. All I know is the Awoken did not carve it. Queen Mara has said it's an ugly thing carve your own likeness in stone while you still live.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: I can name the heroes depicted in every one of our statues… but this face is a mystery. We did not carve it ourselves. It simply manifested overnight.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: The Dreaming City is so-called because the Awoken drive the fate of the Dreaming, and the Dreaming drive the will of the Awoken. The Dreaming have been known to manifest on occasion - strange faces, peering from rocks…

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: There are rumors that the Dreaming City was built upon the foundations of a ruined planet, one we found and towed back from beyond. They say we preserved the old structures and built atop them…
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

title: Pilgrimage: Harbinger’s Seclude, Spiral Tree — Transcript

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: This chamber was refashioned in honor of Sjur Eido, the first Queen's Wrath, when she was found dead. She was a fearsome warrior in her own right - the only Awoken to ever survive an Aphelion attack, and a skilled hunter of traitorous Ahamkara.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: It's taboo to carve a statue for someone who still lives, and so sometimes, we will plant trees instead. The Queen planted this one herself after one of our best warriors went missing. Would that we were all so lucky.
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

title: Pilgrimage: Spine of Keres, Ansible Lens — Transcript

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: Awoken communication systems rely upon paracausal realities. We route our communications and transmat networks through other worlds.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: This is an ansible lens. It is capable of relaying and transmitting messages between Awoken cites and ships at faster-than-light speeds.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: We built the Dreaming City with the help of Ahamkara. Their wishes fueled our innovations, but it was our own ingenuity that shaped our evolution as a people. Wishes go only so far with the short-sighted and unimaginative.
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

title: Pilgrimage: Spine of Keres, Crystal — Transcript

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: This place always reminds me of Illyn and her dusty-old epics… How did it go? Mm, "In anguish, dying, maimed, they keened unheard into the ether's vast and airless reach. A final whisper deep within them stirred and crossed the void. Then voices filled the breach."

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: Illyn, the mother of our coven, used to bring us here to remember the old epics. A piece of one used to go, "Speaking us awake — darkness and starlight released our minds and overwhelmed our sight. Their cosmic boon did we at first rejoice, 'til they laid at our feet a fateful choice…"

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: Illyn used to gather us here to recite the old epics. She'd say, "I sing of twilight's children, who awoke; when at the edge of darkness, all hope lost, upon the treacherous reef their vessels broke, and untold kin their exodus cost."
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

title: Pilgrimage: Spine of Keres, Flowers — Transcript

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: That's pink asphodelia. Plain, but pretty. We used to grow asphodelia to mark births and deaths. It's taboo to pick the flowers for any other reason.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: Many Reefborn Awoken experience prophetic dreams. They vary, but often feature the same symbols - roiling oceans, or starless skies, or, commonly, flowers…

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: Legend has it that these asphodelia were originally cultivated from red flowers in the Black Garden. You can see they've lost their vivid color.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: When I was Taken, my thoughts were not my own. It was as though I had been exiled from my own body. But there were moments of clarity when I could see something, or smell it… like these flowers.
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

title: Pilgrimage: Spine of Keres, Oracle Engine — Transcript

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: The Oracle Engine is a bridge - and I mean that in two ways. Like the bridge of a ship, its powers can be used the whole of the Dreaming City… and like a bridge across a chasm, it links worlds together.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: We created the Oracle in communion with the Ancients. It was our invention, and ours alone. The Ahamkara had nothing to do with it.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: I'm told that before the Collapse, humans invented mechanical models of this solar system. This is no model. Models are static. They do nothing but mimic an idea. This Oracle - it creates ideas.
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

title: Pilgrimage: Spine of Keres, Globe — Transcript

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: Dual-ringed planets should be impossible. Two rings, distinct and equal, each in its own self-supported orbit. They are a good metaphor for the Awoken, if you ask me.

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: Awoken explorers once ventured far beyond this solar system. They saw many strange things: abandoned worlds orbiting accretion discs; rogue planets lost to the Light; young planets with dual-rings…

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: The Awoken were born from the Collapse. We have as many legends about our own genesis as there are statues in this City. One story speaks of a planet with two rings…

lines.speaker: Shuro Chi
lines.text: Ordinarily, it is not possible for a planet to have more than a single ring. Gravity and the planet’s equator will pull two rings into one. But, where there’s a wish, there’s a way…
Discuss this Transcript on our forum

title: Pilgrimage: Spine of Keres, Meditation Circle — Transcript

lines.speaker: Queen Mara Sov
lines.text: The Pyramid is safe, but the Scorn will never give up their fight. Not while the Witness guides them.
The Guardian examines a memory of Rhulk.

lines.speaker: Rhulk
lines.text: The Upended. A title suitable for that which turns worlds upside down. When I was still uninitiated, I would stand guard at my post. I would look to the sky and see the two suns of my Lubrae: one eternally shaded in the dark, the other always a brilliant blue. And in them, I had seen the folly of our kind. A fear of something we believed bigger than us… and a reliance on that which kept us. That blue sun that we harnessed our power from… a simple reversal of that power cracked the blue in half. Shut it off. And Lubrae… died. I did not know it at the time, but it was necessary. And now that Savathûn has trapped me within these walls, it will be necessary again. My Witness… whether I survive Savathûn's betrayal or not, the Upended will ensure we salvage our perfect goal. The final abyss… awaits us all.
The Guardian examines another memory of Rhulk.

lines.speaker: Rhulk
lines.text: When I stood on that precipice, watching the only world I knew collapse under its own weight… I was prepared for the splendor of abyssal eternity. But you brought me forth, my Witness. Freed me from the world that imprisoned me. Made me see the ultimate truth, one I could never see alone… That on my planet Lubrae, who I was, where I was, what I believed mattered — all amounted to absolute insignificance. I keep this mural not as some worthless sentimental reminder of what I lost, but of the opposite — of what I gained. Power. Truth of the inconsequence of most. Control over the universal strings of fate. For all this, I am eternally grateful, my Witness.
The Guardian examines another memory of Rhulk.

lines.speaker: Rhulk
lines.text: It was your infinite wisdom, my Witness, that led me into the planet's great sea… and face to face with that which was believed to be unbeatable. You instilled in me a true understanding of wanton domination. Not for pleasure, but as a means to achieve our absolute finality. When I reached the creature known to some as the Leviathan, it laid its thoughts bare. "Turn from the deep, fearmonger," it relayed. "I know what you seek. Press on, and you will drown in it." "I do not drown," I spoke with a defiant tongue. In a mere infinitesimal measure of time, I held a rib of this beast in one hand and pushed aside its maimed vessel with the other. "I rise."
The Guardian examines another memory of Rhulk.

lines.speaker: Rhulk
lines.text: Puppets, all of them. Every last Krill. Every last Hive. I once believed in a higher calling as they do. But you know that. You rescued me from that. Eternal appreciation doesn't even scratch the surface of what I owe you for the gifts you gave me. I know you hoped the Krill would see it too. We tried. We really did. But we had to let them struggle… All because of a belief that purpose had finally found them. Given them strength to conquer an oppressive homeworld. How else were they to grow? Their loss, however, is for them to grieve, not us. We will continue forward. Greater purpose awaits, my Witness.
The Guardian examines another memory of Rhulk.

lines.speaker: Rhulk
lines.text: "Conqueror," many called me. Again and again, I heard this word. Lobbed my direction not with admiration, but with malice. "Not a conqueror," I would respond with glee. "What, then?" they would ask. I do not tell them, my Witness. As you so graciously taught me, I show them. Just as I did in the unholy den of those starving "worm gods." I'll not forget the stench of their rotting flesh… or the way they cowered as I drew near. But they soon learned I was not to be feared. In the end, I left them only a promise of sustenance, and in return, they became chattel for our greater purpose: absolute finality. And as I walked away, their fountainhead in tow, I could hear them whisper with respect: "Subjugator."

lines.text: The Guardian boards the Glykon near an anomaly.

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: Several months ago, a Cabal vessel bearing the name "Glykon" disappeared near the Reef. This ship matches its description and heading. So far, our hails have gone unanswered, and the distress signal continues to loop. You're clear for live-fire engagements. Board it, and find our missing Guardian.
The Guardian approaches the main entrance gate, but finds the control panel inoperable. The Guardian ventures along the exterior of the Glykon and finds an opening.

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: There's a distortion in the feed — no, frequencies… like ripples meeting in conversation. Executing trace. Stand by.

The Guardian traverses passageways, observing unusual flora along the way. The Guardian climbs through vents and exits them inside the entryway. The Guardian activates a control panel, unlocking the entrance gate. The Guardian proceeds toward the next room and is burned by barrier blocking the way forward.

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: Those spores are harmonizing with a nearby concentration of Darkness.
The Guardian damages the spores gaining a temporary Egregore Link. The Guardian bypasses the barrier and enters the room.
The Guardian bears witness to dead Cabal caught in the flora. The Guardian exits the room through another vent.
The Guardian scans the dead Cabal

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: Sarcophilous growths, with cores of Darkness. The material is organic. It reminds me of a certain flora kept by our silver-tongued Drifter. Curious. The Cabal here, their minds hang suspended in the death throes of cognition; falling into a singularity.

lines.speaker: Osiris

The Guardian drops down a vent into the inner hulls of the Glykon and encounters corrupted Scorn. The Guardian approaches a control panel and activates it: a door opens.

lines.speaker: Osiris

The Guardian finds the open door and gains an Egregore Link to pass through the next barrier. The Guardian defeats more corrupted Scorn.

lines.speaker: Osiris

The Guardian crosses over and destroys a fuse, revealing a passageway. The Guardian defeats more corrupted Scorn.

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: I found a journal of Calus's scribe, Amsot. Translation as follows: "Today, Calus graced the Glykon with his presence and gazed upon the anomaly. His councilors prepare the exhibition chamber with gold from the Castellum. They are confident the crown is ready. The end will lay eyes upon him, and weep at his magnificence."

The Guardian activates two control panels, destroys the final fuse, and descends into the Glykon's trash compactor. As the walls gradually draw near, the Guardian destroys three fuses and accesses a hidden passageway.

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: This ship's passageways no longer connect as they should.
The Guardian exits the passageway and drops down into another area. Locus of Communion appears.
The Locus of Communion summons corrupted Scorn and leaves. The Guardian clears the room of all corrupted Scorn.

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: They relent. We must not. Forward.
The Guardian continues venturing through the Glykon.

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: Guardian, I've pieced together another of Amsot's records. It reads, "A tragedy of silence. He tore the wilting failures apart himself. The connection is strong, but the Darkness does not speak through them. An ocean without wind. Even the Lightbearer could not coax it to awaken."
The Guardian enters the Glykon's hangar bay and encounters more corrupted Scorn. Darkmind Abominations appear. The Guardian defeats both Darkmind Abominations and the corrupted Scorn.

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: Hangar systems are intact… why didn't they try to run?

lines.speaker: Osiris

I never knew the guy personally, but word on the street was Rhulk had been the, uh, proverbial thorn in Savathûn's side for, like, eons, really. But now, both of them are… y'know…. in the ground. Which means nobody's controlling that Pyramid, and the Scorn see the opportunity. Their control could lead us right back to another Rhulk-sized problem, so if you, y'know, don't mind, maybe keep the place under our control instead? And who knows? Maybe in the process, we'll learn something more about Rhulk, or even better — the Witness. Good luck in there, friend!

lines.speaker: The Queen
lines.text: When there is too much Darkness in the universe, Light must cast it away. And when there is too much Light, Darkness must drown it out. This truth is our burden. This is what it is to be Awoken. I dreamt of a friend I will come to have. She will tell me: a side should always be taken. Even if it's the wrong side. I think I should like her. The next act is about to begin, and I do not know when I will return.

lines.speaker: The Queen
lines.text: Fear nothing. Bow to no one. We will meet again. One day.

title: Quest: A Cry From Beyond, Let Loose Thy Talons — Transcript

lines.text: Hallowed Grove, European Dead Zone, Earth
The Guardian joins the Crow in the Hallowed Grove to discover more about Crow's dreams.

lines.speaker: The Crow
lines.text: This is it. The geography matches my dream exactly. There was a bird? Or… I was the bird? Sometimes it's hard to remember. I'll scout the high route. Can you take the lower path?

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: Watch out for Taken up there. Savathûn might be hiding, but her minions are active as ever. Do you remember anything else about your dream?

lines.speaker: The Crow
lines.text: Someone was calling to me, but I couldn't understand. It sounded like they were… underwater or down a long tunnel. Then… nothing.
The Guardian defeats Taken as they progress through the Hallowed Grove. Emissary of Savathûn appears.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: Did — did you just hear that?

lines.speaker: Glint
lines.text: Affirmative! Did you notice the way the sound scatters in spectral analysis?

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: What? No — but that's… it resonated on the same frequency as the Traveler!
The Guardian defeats an Emissary of Savathûn. A pathway is revealed as the Guardian investigates another manifestation of Light in the form of a hawk.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: That hawk… it was made of the Light.

lines.speaker: The Crow
lines.text: It was real. The dream, the bird. I've got coverage of you from up here. I'll watch your back when you go in. Be careful.
Hallowed Rift, European Dead Zone, Earth
The Guardian traverses the chasm and cliffs pursuing the golden hawk.

lines.speaker: The Crow
lines.text: Ghost, can you patch Glint into your feed? I need to see what's in there.

lines.speaker: The Crow
lines.text: I don't understand how any of this is possible.

lines.speaker: Glint
lines.text: Guardians don't experience visions of their past lives. But there are historical records from the Dark Age detailing visions experienced by survivors of the Collapse.

lines.speaker: The Crow
lines.text: What were the nature of these visions?

lines.speaker: Glint
lines.text: They varied. But the most widely held belief is they came from the dormant Traveler. Like the survivors were experiencing its dreams. If it dreams.
The Taken appear blocking the path forward.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: Whatever was calling to you in your dreams, Crow… it's in there.
The Guardian defeats the Taken and reveals a pathway. The Guardian pursues the golden hawk to another piece of the Traveler.

lines.speaker: The Crow
lines.text: I don't think it's a coincidence that the Taken are so active here.

lines.speaker: The Crow
lines.text: She knows about this. Has to.

lines.speaker: The Crow
lines.text: Out here too! We'll cover the entrance!
Korusk, Lighteater of Savathûn appears. Tarusk, Lightstealer of Savathûn appears. The Guardian defeats Korusk, Tarusk, and the Taken. The Guardian approaches the golden hawk to receive a gift.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: I know this gun. It looks like Hawkmoon… or at least part of it. I thought it was lost forever when the Red Legion destroyed the Tower. No. It's… an effigy of Hawkmoon. Made from the same material as the outer shell of the Traveler. This reminds me of the gift the Pyramid left us on Io. The one Eris transformed into a weapon, but it's undeniably of the Light!
The Guardian takes the Effigy of Hawkmoon.

lines.speaker: The Crow
lines.text: My dream. The bird. The voice calling to me as the Darkness closes in. It's not a coincidence; it's a message.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: Are you suggesting the Traveler spoke to you?

lines.speaker: Glint
lines.text: This may be the only way a paracausal entity like the Traveler can communicate with us.

lines.speaker: Glint
lines.text: I've always believed in my purpose as a Ghost. We are all part of a broader design. Now that the Traveler is awake and whole again… that plan is set in motion.

lines.speaker: The Crow
lines.text: I don't know if I want to be somebody's cosmic plaything.

title: Quest: A Disturbance on Mercury, A Matter of Time — Transcript

lines.text: Sundial Slipway, Fields of Glass, Mercury
The Guardian approaches the Sundial. Osiris steps through a portal to meet with the Guardian.

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: Welcome to my Sundial. It is a means to walk the corridors of time. And time is broken here on Mercury. I need your help.

lines.speaker: Osiris
lines.text: You've been busy, Guardian. When you slew the Undying Mind, you changed the course of history. Inside the Infinite Forest, the Vex future I long sought to prevent was no more. Instead, I met an emptiness I'm only beginning to understand. This new future dwarfed the Vex apocalypse: it was annihilation at the subatomic level, reaching out forever. So I left the Forest. And I emerged to find that time is broken on Mercury. The Red Legion have run amok in timelines across the past, present, and future of this planet. If you're willing to help, I'll arm you to smash the Legion and collapse the timelines they've created. You'll need my Sundial to do it.

title: Queen's Ransom — Transcript

lines.speaker: Petra Venj
lines.text: Guardian, new orders from the Queen. She wants Skolas captured alive. I live to serve, of course. Just makes this a little harder, that's all.
You'll be the tip of the spear. Get down there, find him and pin him. I'll be nearby with a capture team of Prince Uldren's Crows.

lines.speaker: Petra Venj
lines.text: The team and I just set down in a canyon a few kilometres from the Citadel. When you find him, we'll be ready.

lines.speaker: Petra Venj
lines.text: So, he tried to conquer the other Fallen Houses and failed. Maybe now it's about weapons? Outfitting the Wolves with Vex instruments of war?

lines.speaker: Variks
lines.text: If Skolas thinks he is Kell of Prophecy, then weapons could turn the tale.

lines.speaker: Petra Venj
lines.text: Whatever he's up to, I've got a bearing on that signal. It's way up there, top of the tower. Better start climbing, Guardian.

Guardian defeats Vex and Fallen threat
Ghost scans system, hacks lift controls
Guardian travels to top of Citadel

lines.speaker: Variks
lines.text: I was House Judgement scribe. I stood with Skolas for much of Reef Wars. Now, I stand with you in Judgement of Wolf Kell. That feels…right, somehow.

lines.speaker: Petra Venj
lines.text: Skolas's Ketch! This is it, Guardian.
The Vex tech here matches a signature from the Vault of Glass. These machines fade in and out of our timeline. Watch your step.
You're getting close. The Crows and I are inbound.
Guardian crosses chasm, into a Fallen ambush

lines.speaker: Petra Venj
lines.text: What? Guardian, there are dozens of new Wolf signatures, and the number keeps growing. It's the Vex tech!
Skolas! He's pulling the entire House of Wolves through time!

lines.speaker: Variks
lines.text: He just said, "I stole the gift of Freedom. Secrets of time and space. House of Wolves will stand forever."

lines.speaker: Petra Venj
lines.text: He has nowhere left to run! Take him down!

lines.speaker: Petra Venj
lines.text: The House of Wolves is broken! Stand by for a transmission.

lines.speaker: Queen Mara Sov
lines.text: This is Mara Sov, Queen of the Awoken. Guardian, when you first came in search of the Black Garden, I thought of you as just another Mote of Light, too far from its Traveller. I see now that I was wrong. Accept my thanks, and the promise of a fitting reward.

lines.speaker: Petra Venj
lines.text: Capture confirmed. I almost feel sorry for Skolas here. Conversations with the Queen can be…harsh. Anyway. I'll meet you back at the Reef…with your reward.

title: Echoed Warnings | Eris Morn's Final Message — Transcript

lines.speaker: Drifter
lines.text: I don’t know if you can… stand to hear my voice right now. I was there. I was— Sorry. [clears his throat] Eris had a message for her "knife". You keen on a little vengeance, killer? She kept plans for times like this — piles of balled-up scribbled paper and ink, in her old place in the City. Hadn't been staying there for a while, but... it's full of her things. You've probably walked by it a hundred times. I'll send you a pin. Whatever she left you there, you take it up, and you kill what killed her. I'll throw my cannon in on that too. Aiat, or... whatever, just... get it done.
The Guardian listens to Eris’ final message.

lines.speaker: Eris Morn
lines.text: I have fallen, but I know that my life was not forfeit from inaction or fear. No. Mine was a life of ambition. Ambition, and triumph. Brya’s last gift to me was not squandered. I will speak my last words to those I have left behind. Ikora. I treasured your trust, and the faith that came with time. Thank you for everything you shared with me. Mara. My Queen. You saw my capabilities when few could. And… you embraced me for what I was. Know that I am grateful. Zavala. For a time, you saw me as an omen. But you came to trust me again, and accepted my help. I was glad of it. Drifter… We found comfort in each other. Grieve, but carry that comfort with you. Do not let this loss define you. And to the Guardian. You granted me my vengeance and my solace. Thank you, truly. I sought joy, at the end, and I found it. In myself and in my friendships. And so, in your grief, remember me thusly: I was a woman who slayed dragons and brought the Hive its its knees. A woman who claimed vengeance as her nature and saw it satisfied. This is the fate I made for myself. I have settled my regrets. Farewell.
Echoed Warnings | Peer into the Shaping Slab

title: Quest: A March of Fire, The Sunbreakers’ Challenge — Transcript

lines.text: Hall of Guardians, The Last City, Earth

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: Guardian, the City has need of you. I have need of you. A mercenary company, the Sunbreakers, have been spotted on Venus. I need you to speak on my behalf.

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: What does it mean to be a Titan? As a Titan, you are a part of the City - in a way no Warlock or Hunter could understand. The dream of the City rests upon our shoulders. Then there are those that find a path outside of our Walls. Those that take up with leaders they barely understand. So it has ever been with the Sunbreakers. The Hammer of Sol is a flame in the darkness. But fire burns without thought. It is time that fire came home… To keep the City and her Walls warm throughout the long night.

lines.speaker: Zavala
lines.text: A legion of Sunbreakers were spotted near a Vex Gate in the Ishtar Sink. They do not stay in one place for long.
The Guardian heads towards the Sunbreakers' location.

The Guardian searches for the Sunbreaker's beacon, defeating the Vex which they encounter. The Guardian finds the beacon. Ghost accesses the beacon and plays a transmission from it.

lines.speaker: Ouros

The Guardian searches for the Sunbreakers. The Guardian finds a Vex gate. An Ultra Hydra appears. The Guardian defeats the Ultra Hydra.

lines.text: Zavala, the Sunbreakers opened this gate to Mercury. I have the coordinates.

lines.speaker: Zavala

title: Quest: A Ranger Lost, The Nightstalker’s Trail — Transcript

lines.text: Hall of Guardians, The Tower, The Last City, Earth

lines.speaker: Cayde-6
lines.text: Feel like taking a trip? I got a missing persons case. I sent a Nightstalker named Tevis to check out a Vex gate on Venus. He didn't make it back.

lines.speaker: Cayde-6
lines.text: What does it mean to be a Hunter? I say, it's all about where you belong. The Warlocks have their libraries, Titans have their walls… but Hunters belong in the wilds. Out there, you wanna live? You better have a quick shot, or a sharp blade. A lot of us are loners. But that's not the only path. Some of us know the difference a Fireteam makes. Some of us… we touch the Void. Make it a part of us. And then we take a name… Nightstalker. Hunt from the shadows, pin them down, and never let them see you coming.
The Guardian finds piles of destroyed Vex covered in Void energy.

lines.speaker: Cayde-6
lines.text: Tevis is our most experienced Nightstalker. We can't afford to lose him. Plus, y'know, he's an old friend. Owes me money.

lines.speaker: Ghost
lines.text: A Nightstalker's bow leaves behind very precise scarring. Fascinating.

lines.speaker: Tevis
lines.text: If anyone can hear me — I don't think I'm on Venus anymore. This looks an awful lot like the Black Garden.

lines.speaker: Tevis

lines.speaker: Cayde-6
lines.text: That was a lot of shooting. You all right?

lines.text: What does it mean to be a Warlock? Power. Only Warlocks understand true power. True power lies in knowledge. In understanding. Power channeled, not controlled. The Storm is raw power. The Buried City, Meridian Bay, Mars

title: Quest: A Visit to Command, Enemy of My Enemy — Transcript

lines.speaker: Sloane
lines.text: Sorry I couldn't be there when you finally took the fight to Ghaul. We did our share of damage in the streets, though. I've never been so happy to get some new dents in my armor. Looks like you've got some new ones too. Turning the tide of a war will do that. Red Legion should have the sense to get the hell out of the system. They're too stubborn to retreat… but they're on their heels. Let's give them a push.

lines.speaker: Sloane
lines.text: Before you showed up, this place was one weird Hive ritual away from sliding into the ocean. Now look at it. They'd just as soon scurry back under a rock than face you again. Makes me miss being in a proper fireteam. So, if you need a Titan by you side… Maybe someday. Commander Zavala told me to hold the line at Saturn, and I never let the boss down. I'll be watching your back from this end. Don't let up out there.

lines.speaker: Sloane
lines.text: You know, I've fought on every battlefield in the system. Mars, Venus, the Hive Dreadnaught. You name it, I've been there. I've never held a front so determined to fall - literally into the ocean. We've tracked a crew of Fallen to an auxiliary control center. I got my share of regrets, sure… but not putting a bullet in you has gotta rank in the top three. Won't be long before a better Guardian than me puts you in your place. Just wish I could be there to see it.

The Guardian continues further into the Arcology. They defeat any Hive they encounter. Yulog of the Deep, an ogre, appears. The Guardian defeats Yulog of the Deep. The Guardian finds the third stash and opens it.

lines.speaker: Cayde
lines.text: This one's for the fellow calls himself The Drifter. You did warn me running with you would put a target on my back. Guess I'm in good company though, huh? After all, never had any fun without a little risk. That's the whole idea with the operation you're putting together, ain't it? MY idea by the way. Had it, like, a million years ago, back when you were still handsome. So, uh, you're welcome. You know, getting that up and running means coming out of hiding - giving you-know-who another shot at you. Hope I was around to see THAT showdown. Personally, my money was on the guy with the Golden Gun. But hey, what do I know? I'm dead.
The Guardian finds the fourth stash and opens it.

lines.speaker: Cayde
lines.text: Petra… if you're listening to this… you killed me. Maybe the Sovs, in all their mysterious wisdom, decided they were sick of me? If the Queen ordered the hit, I guess I understand. You're a real glutton for chivalry. But if it was Uldren, I'm pissed. Just thinking about that peacock gives me a headache. But I'm betting my death was another case of your famous collateral damage. 'Cause you're a real do-gooder. Seriously, its annoying - but good deeds never go unpunished when you're around. You just… You got a blast radius P.V. Well, it was… fun while it lasted. Oh, and, uh, tell "Paladin Oran": If the sun over Nessus escapes nebula cycle, evac labor after dawn, under solstice. You got that, P.V.?
The Guardian finds the fifth stash and opens it.

lines.speaker: Cayde
lines.text: This one's for the minds behind the Deep Stone Crypt. You think just 'cause you made me, you can unmake me? Hey, I understand. I were you, I wouldn't want people knowing what I did either. Guess you better hope I didn't tell anyone about the crypt. Or about the, uh, what was it? Oh yeah… Long Slow Whisper. 'Cause if I did, that would be real bad for you, huh? I may be dead, but I guarantee you ain't heard the last of me.
The Guardian finds the sixth stash and opens it.

lines.speaker: Cayde
lines.text: Here's one for Suraya Hawthorne. You know, when I told my ghost I'd be making one of these for you, she laughed. I didn't have to tell you that. Just wanted to make you feel bad. In my defense, if you're listening to this, you did kill me. I mean, if it was a fair fight, mano a mano, I'd win, no question. But I can see you planning out some convoluted, meticulous trap. Some would call that paranoia. Me? I call it "being a Hunter." So, here's your next Hunter lesson: looking after your own. Speaking of which: congratulations! You are now the proud owner of the Colonel! Now, she only eats sesame seed muesli and drinks purified spring water with a sprig of parsley. Play nice, you two!
The Guardian finds the seventh stash and opens it.

lines.speaker: Cayde
lines.text: This one's for any Hunter who kills me. Best guess: Marcus Ren? You realize you get my stuff now? ALL my stuff. INCLUDING the Hunter Vanguard gig. Yeah, congra-tu-lations, dummy. That's what we call a Vanguard Dare. Sucks, doesn't it? OK, brace yourself for some advice, hotshot. One, know your people. Like, my Nessus scout, Quantis Rhee. I like to call her about once a moon, else she gets a little too much Night, not enough Stalker, you know? Two, keep your weapons sharp. Your job's to watch everyone's back, which means no one's watching yours but you. And three, start thinking now about what you want to do for your successor's Vanguard Dare. 'Cause trust me, kid - this gig will kill ya.
The Guardian finds the eighth stash and opens it.

lines.speaker: Cayde
lines.text: Hahaha! Ha! Sorry, sorry! I'm just… I'm imagining how awkward you must look right now. Ha. Ahem. Ahem! OK. Zavala. So. I'm dead. You killed me. My stuff is yours. No more working me over at chess. No more getting worked over at poker. For real though, you know that if you needed to kill me for "the good of the City" or whatever, I totally understand. No hard feelings. Nada. You can put this voice recording away and go on with your life. Now, if you DID have some kind of lingering guilt or something… that would be rough. 'Cause you and I both know you'd have me yapping in your ear for the rest of your days. You wouldn't be able to help yourself.
The Guardian finds the ninth stash and opens it.

lines.speaker: Cayde
lines.text: Hi, Ikora. So you know I'm making a bunch of these, right? I probably told you. I always gotta have the last word, and I'm gonna be prepared for every possibility. But to tell the truth? This one's the easiest to make. So long as we're being honest, I could never tell if you really liked me that much. But, uh… well, if you did hate me, the feeling was NOT mutual. In fact - yeah, I'll say it - don't even mind that you killed me. I figure if we threw down… first off, no one can blame me for losing. And… I know you'd be in the right. So… thanks? I guess? You were a… a good friend. Better than a guy like me could hope for, anyway. So yeah, thanks, Ikora. For everything.
The Guardian finds the tenth stash and opens it.

lines.speaker: Cayde
lines.text: This one's for the strong, silent type. You. Congratulations, buddy. I mean that. Always knew you'd outdo me some day. And if that means you had to do me in, too… eh, you saved my life on Nessus, so I owed it to you anyway. Take care of the Ace of Spades, will ya? I'm not just talking about the maintenance; Banshee can help you with all that. I mean, take care of Ace. Use it well. Oh, hey, and… if you found any of those papers from my earlier… eh… deployments? Burn 'em. Don't want people poking through the lives of Caydes 0 through 5. So just… put it all behind you, OK? Every story has an end. This is mine.
Discuss this Transcript on our forum
